Three tolls of the bell sounded. One by one, the people at the gathering removed their hats and stepped forward to place fresh flowers into the cold coffin.
Some wept quietly, others bowed their heads in silence. Rozzan scanned the surroundings, but he didn't spot that familiar crimson figure anywhere.
The last of the Elder Wolves who survived the incident laid in the casket. He spent the rest of his days in pain. Though the Bonekrusher's haze ravaged his organs and their blades pierced his limbs, the Elder Wolf held on tightly to the swaddled young pup ... until he passed her into the arms of another boy...
"She's still not here..."
The words reached Rozzan. He gave a slow nod, then quietly passed the rest of the service over to another Elder.
He knew where to find her. Whenever she was upset, she'd lose herself in the training grounds and stay there until late into the night.
Rozzan watched the girl in silence. She noticed him too, but neither said a word. With one last fierce thrust, she drove her sword into the training dummy and collapsed to the ground. No one knew how long she had been pushing herself here.
"He's gone."
Rozzan approached Rossi where she lay gasping on the ground, his voice quiet and flat.
"I know... I know..."
Rossi pulled her hood down over her eyes, but her voice shook uncontrollably. Ever since she was old enough to understand, she had visited the wounded Old Wolf every single week so he could see that she was growing up strong and well. To her, he was the last living thread connecting her to those lost souls.
"You should have been there. He would have wanted you there."
"But ... it was because of me... He did it all for..."
Rozzan hoisted her up and slung her over his shoulder before she could finish, carrying her toward the courtyard where the funeral was being held.
"I can't face him ... it was all my fault... I don't want to..."
Rossi thrashed and bit against Rozzan's shoulder. Her nails scraped his skin, her teeth sank into his arm. Rozzan's expression didn't flicker. He just kept walking toward the funeral.
Soon, Rossi's strength gave out. She slumped against Rozzan's back, arms hanging limp.
"I didn't become the wolf the Pack could rely on..."
Rossi murmured, unsure if she was speaking to Rozzan, or to someone no longer there.
"I never learned to stand on my own. I couldn't lead anyone. I haven't done a single thing right... I didn't deserve their sacrifice..."
Rozzan came to a stop. The courtyard was empty now, save for the ashes of burnt offerings and a solitary coffin. Inside, the elder lay peacefully, covered in flowers.
"Every time you came to see him, he'd always pull me aside afterward to talk. Maybe age caught up to the wolf and he never remembered what he told me. Just kept ranting the same stories on and on."
Rozzan set Rossi down. He rested a hand on the edge of the coffin, gazing at his old friend.
"He'd always go on about the glory days, the few times we butted heads. But the details ... those kept changing. One day he was the one who messed up, the next it was me. The same story was told different every time. Only one thing he ever said never changed."
Rozzan reached over and ruffled Rossi's hair.
"Every single time, he'd say that saving you was the greatest thing he ever did."
Rossi lowered her head. She took off the pale pendant from around her neck, the one the elder had given her, and placed it among the flowers.
The coffin sealed. The young wolf never cried again.

Operator Da Pan (ID name: Pan Yuan) is a member of the Hongshan Academy of Sciences (HAS). He claims to be a very well-traveled chef and trader. He has joined the Specialist Tech Division as an independent, with recommendations from Operator Chen Qianyu and a letter of authentication from HAS. We also respected his personal wishes and granted him partial authority levels for canteen access. 

Da Pan provided an incredibly chaotic CV. His verifiable work experiences include: owner of hot pot eatery, LA-ME-DA (literal translation: Spicily Huge); tianshi at HAS; electrician; carpenter; machinist; and background extra in Heyi Quan: Zailin (literal translation: Fist of Combined Will: Revisited). 
Two of his past experiences cannot be verified. The first was a brief stint of driving taxis at Simonch. We failed to find any commercial driving license or records for Da Pan in the said city. When I pointed out this finding, the Ursus' maw cracked into a 70-degree smile and he applied a rather powerful slap on my mechanical chassis. The second would be "friendly assists and support". Da Pan claims he part-timed as an ornamental burdenbeast stand-in for three days at La Fantoma. By the time I realized that I had been misled into an engrossing dialog about unlicensed taxi driving and ornamental burdenbeasts, we had already been talking for four hours — and I had neglected to ask Da Pan about the experiences that he should remember best: his time as a tianshi at HAS. 
While verifying his experiences in HAS, Da Pan became visibly downcast and displeased. But he quickly resumed his smile and deflected the topic with a casual joke. Then he showed me a friendly group photo of him and other ornamental burdenbeasts. I could obviously tell that he was trying to avoid talking about his disagreeable past with other Tianshi, but this is not a negative consideration for Endfield. Since Da Pan is still affected by the Science Station incident, it proves that he remains, deep inside, a HAS tianshi who upholds a strong sense of principles, responsibilities, and duty. 
— Martin Marvin Malen, Assistant, HR Division, Endfield Industries

-4297975222758153993:
After the fall of Sami, most of the Sami people accepted the outcome. They live atop the Feranmut's remains, carrying on His will, fighting the Aggelos to protect Talos-II.
Yet there were still Snowpriests who believed that Sami had not truly died. His soul had merely been lost within the rifts, fallen into a deep slumber. One day, Sami would wake from His dream and return to His people. They traveled to the rifts across Talos-II, setting up altars and performing rituals, trying to call Sami's soul back from the fissures. But none who went ever returned. Later, with the northern front growing ever more urgent, no one was willing to continue the attempt.
In a snowy forest near the Wuling Very Large Rift, Typhoeus found the manuscripts left behind by one of those Sami Snowpriests. The manuscripts detailed all her attempts to awaken Sami. Though Typhoeus was able to confirm through her own exploration that the ritual had failed and the Snowpriestess had vanished without a trace, the girl still caught a faint whiff of possibility from the remaining materials.
Unfortunately, after months of study, Typhoeus had made no progress.
She asked every Snowpriest and shaman in the Order of Steel Oath and Myrkwood, but they all just shook their heads, believing it to be a doomed endeavor.
Even after hitting so many dead ends, Typhoeus did not lose heart. The Snowpriestess's unique insights on dreams in the manuscripts taught the girl to perceive special revelations within the dreamscapes of others.

"I don't know why, but lately I keep dreaming of being chased by a gigantic monster. The ground beneath my feet keeps swaying, as if I am standing on a suspension bridge. I toss and turn all night long..."
"Simple. That monster is hunting you, and you have been cornered."
"What should I do?"
"Become stronger. Do not be the prey. Be the hunter instead."
"I think I get it now."

After that conversation with Typhoeus, the operator mapped out a full month of intensive training for himself. The exhaustion and sense of accomplishment from the workouts let him sleep soundly through the night. Before long, Endfield colleagues began showing up at Typhoeus's door with all sorts of dreams, asking her to read and interpret them.
And Typhoeus, after listening to everyone's dreams, drew inspiration from them to craft a legend of her own, one that wove together the Feranmut Sami, dreams, and the Snowpriests.
Soon, Typhoeus finished writing the ending. She thought the matter would settle just like the story itself. So she gathered her notes and set off to share the conclusion with those who had been waiting eagerly. But halfway there, she brushed past a young girl in the corridor.
Typhoeus did not recognize her, yet she felt a strangely familiar presence emanating from her.
It was a presence that had accompanied her people through swamps and forests, through winters and into springs, from birth all the way to death.
By the time Typhoeus came to her senses, the girl had already walked far away.
Later, she learned from others the girl's codename: Last Rite.
Driven by a mysterious premonition, she tore out the ending she had written and wrote that codename on a fresh page instead.

[AUDIO LOG EXCERPT 1]
"AHEM— Talosian Calendar Year 15, ██ of ██. Day three after moving into the temporary shelters... QUIET, TORY! You're supposed to fix the chair, not bring down the house!
"Quit nagging already. And enough yapping about your fine studio at downtown Wrankwood. Hell, even I like a hot water bath and trashy movies to go along with it. But clean towels are a luxury now, okay?
"Oh, why don't you heard north, find 'Mr. Angels', take him out for a drink, and ask where his blighted kind hid the keys to the Cosmic Gate? —OF COURSE I KNOW IT DOESN'T EXIST. Where did your sense of humor go? Blown to pieces along with the stabilizer and the blighted Aggeloi?
"What am I doing? I'm making an audio log. Say, how about lending me that camcorder of yours? Your documentary project is on a temporary hold, right...? No? Fine. Blighted camera crew and their pride.
"Where was I again? Oh, yes. Today is Talosian Calendar Year 15—"

[AUDIO LOG EXCERPT 2]
"Dallied around for two weeks and still no news about the others. Murray, Ellie, Henry... I think they're still alive. I gotta keep thinking positive.
"We're one of the lucky ones. At least we got a roof here. The other shelters are jam-packed of people. They told me the war is over but there's no heading back to Terra. Meals are getting worse, too. Sheesh...
"...You're back? Wait. What the hell is that? A sword? You traded a can-o-food for a friggin' razor?! Are you friggin' nuts...?! Oh yeah, great! It killed a buggerloid! So what? Your backup camera almost got one of those buggers too —— KYAA! STOP! I'm sorry! It was my fault!
"You heard Ellie and Murray ended up at the shelters organized by the United Workers' HQ? Awesome. But I heard they have some serious hunger games going on at that place. I heard the UW is meeting up with the Corporate Security Council to talk about some 'shelter program'. Hah. This reminds me of the friggin' boring news on Terra. Never thought I would actually start reading these articles.
"Just ... try to stay here, Tory. Enough scavenging and trading already. Save your pitiful rations.
"And try to check your camcorder... Why? I don't know. I just ... just kinda feel we might get to use it again."

[AUDIO LOG EXCERPT III]
"Hmm... how long has it been? I hardly kept count. Maybe more than five months, maybe?
"Tory and I are now part of the Corporate Security Council entourage — Temporary, of course. We just tag along for a chance to get some worthy footage.
"So this entourage just got demolished yesterday. While beating the retreat, they ran into another equally ragtag band. Turned out to be peeps from the UW. Both sides got into some staring match for half a minute or so. Nobody said anything, but nobody reached for their weapons either. They just ... walked past each other. It felt so friggin' funny — but I couldn't even laugh during that encounter.
"We don't wanna fight, and they don't wanna fight either. But this war lasted more than five months. Why? Tory, got anything to say?
"Oh, right! Tory's out to get some footage. I told him to stick around but he won't listen. I kinda admire how he could still pick up his camcorder. I for one, got no idea why I'm recording anything and I don't feel like it anymore. Nobody's gonna watch our documentaries. But maybe Tory's right. Someone's gotta record the dumb crap and blightery that's going on.
"And oh yes, Tory's can-for-a-sword is still around. It's the reason why we're still breathing. I heard its OG owner was fighting too. Poor dude got un-alived because he refused to point his weapon at a pardner during the Aggeloi War. HAH! Now I'm laughing. Maybe I'm really mad.
"Crap! Crap! CRAP! It's starting again! Who's fighting who? I don't know. I never figured it out.
"...Blight this blightery. Where the hell is Tory?"

[VIDEO FOOTAGE (Blurry)]
"—HAHA! UP YOURS! We won, pardner! Our war friggin' drove the heavens MAD!! This is an Originium Catastrophe with CAPITAL C! The first of its kind on Talos-II! And we got ourselves some exclusive footage! LOOK, TORY!! It's exactly like what we got on Terra! See it, Tory?! You should be here, with me! Our reel will be nabbing tons of serious awards, Tory! NAME! Give our documentary a name, Tory! Lemme think... OH YES! Call it EFFIN' GLORIOUS MEMORY! That's super rad! We are SOOOOO totally gonna win those bling-bling trophies!
"OH! CHECK THAT OUT! That blighted tower is coming down — THERE! A perfect concluding shot! CONGRATULATIONS, HUMANITY!!"

-2668066955091880080:
"Endfield is a legitimate enterprise. You need to learn to distinguish fact from rumor. Not all those legends are true."
Every time a new employee joins Endfield, the veteran staff makes a point of reminding them of this.
That was until Operator Typhoeus joined Endfield, and all that effort went down the drain. With her rambling, mystical tales, this girl blurred the line between rumor and reality, turning us from a company with a certain legendary flair into ... a legend, plain and simple.
The mysterious characters flashing across the screens, the crying sounds echoing from the bridge late at night, the lighting fixtures in the Engineering Division that never seem to stay fixed, always flickering on and off when someone is alone. These little coincidences, easily dismissed with a laugh, were gathered and woven together by Typhoeus into a spine-chilling legend.

Long ago, the equipment aboard the sky vessel Dijiang was constantly breaking down. The poor craftsmen had no choice but to take shelter in the workshop, forging and repairing day and night without rest. Yet after a full year of toil, the number of machines awaiting repair only grew, piling up around them like an unbroken mountain range.
Consumed by rage, his last shred of kindness was spent. He transformed into a vengeful spirit and entered the machinery itself, vowing to take revenge on every careless soul who cut corners in their operations.
The lights flickering in the night are the sign of his patrol.
— An entry from Typhoeus's notebook.

After this story spread across Dijiang, the number of damage reports on the Engineering Division's repair list for that month dropped significantly.
After looking into the matter, the stunned Mr. Andre gave a fair assessment of the story: this was not a story, but an indisputable fact.
And this was just one chapter among the many legends Typhoeus had written for Endfield. In her notebook, the Endministrator was the great sage holding the Stone of Origin, Supervisor Perlica was the lightning mage wielding the power of thunder, Miss Chen was a ranger carrying a longsword. And everything Endfield did on Talos-II was planting great stone swords across the land to maintain peace in the world and protect all living things.
A twelve-year-old child would find these tales childish, but for the Endfield operators with their heads full of whimsy, they were just right.
"When I am working now, I imagine myself as a mysterious Sami Snowpriest. When the equipment overheats, I shout out ancient invocations..." And with that, Andre picked up the cooling gun from the corner, aimed it at the machine, and cried out, "O wind and snow, descend upon the mortal world!"

-3962614875749143351:
The city had many families. No one knew which of these families was the most friendly and harmonious. But everybody agreed that the Webers were the antithesis of peace. Rarely has there been a family with so many children and so many feuds. Only one Weber should be present in an area of sixty-four square klicks. If more Webers were present, the unfortunate land would soon witness violence and bloodshed.
Just last month, the eldest of the Weber children received a letter on the battlefield. After butchering the enemy who stood before him, he found his officer and applied for one-month of leave and embarked on a journey home. He crossed the woodlands and found his younger brother who was about to bury the axe into the elder Weber's head when the latter suddenly read the contents of the letter. The younger Weber tossed the axe, packed a few things, and joined his brother on a long journey.
Their sister was already waiting on a boat moored at the riverbank. The Weber boys were wary of the massive oar she wielded. Last time they were careless and woke up three days later.
Time was running out but they still had a lengthy journey ahead.
The three siblings faced a vast desert. When they were lost amongst the dunes of ever-changing shapes, a convoy arrived on time. The driver of the lead vehicle lowered the window and revealed a face they all despised and hated beyond all measure — Uncle Weber who lived miles away but never failed to show up and gloat at the family whenever they met difficulties.
"Hop on, brats," Uncle Weber offered a ride to the young Webers and ignored how they rolled their eyes. The other vehicles in the convoy honked and rushed them along. The frustrated cacophony undoubtedly hid a great number of Webers as well.
The convoy started off at once and left ephemeral trails upon the sands. They drove all through the night and day before finally arriving at the final stop. The lake was at peak water level, swollen by a storm that threw great waves crashing at its banks. Thankfully, the richest of their aunts owned a strong, majestic ship capable of accommodating every single Weber.
Aunt Weber the Captain proudly strolled the rolling decks as the ship tore through the storm and rode the waves, giving snorts of disdain to every Weber who failed to keep their stomach juices in, and grunts of contempt to the discolored Webers who held on to the railings for dear life. The tempest accompanied them throughout the journey, and all the Webers arrived at their homeland safely.
Everyone was shocked to see the Webers charging across the main avenue for the biggest hospital in town. There were so many of them that they covered the entire length of the road.
And the Webers finally gathered at the ward and surrounded a baby girl still in her wrappings. The infant weakly opened her eyes and looked at everyone present before closing them forever, untouched and untainted by the mundane affairs of the mortal world.
"Thank you for agreeing to see her one last time," the youngest of the Weber girls said softly as she cuddled the child whose body grew colder and colder.

-3675220694833104674:
The Sarkaz sat in a circle upon the soft, mushy snow. They had discussed the same problems multiple times for the past few months. Tactics for dealing with the ubiquitous Aggeloi, how many soldiers they should send to search and rescue the other races who were inept in fighting, and how they should live with the collapse of the Cosmic Gate and the fact that they would never see Kazdel again. 
The Aggeloi were like an unending flood. The swarming host covered every road, forced them out of the northern frontier outposts, and sent them on a desperate retreat. Once again they became roamers. A people without a future in sight, and without a way back to their homeworld. 
The sunlight reflecting off the great rings of the gas giant grew dimmer by the day. The walls became increasingly caked in blood, and food reserves ran low. The air grew stale and suffocating as fewer people had ideas to share. The Sarkaz remained silent, even when the Samifjod shared their goodwill. 
But this day was different, thought Fleming. Everyone must say something, so he broke the silence first. "Do we have a conclusion on that Feranmut tooth? Turn it into another Lifebone?" 
"I don't get it. Why give us a thing of such great value?" 
"Because we offered them crucial military support, maybe?" 
There was a brief pause. "But the Feranmut fell anyways." 
"Their Snowpriests mentioned a prophecy about us..." 
Confusion and uncertainty still saturated their words, but there was progress, however slow it was. Fleming tried to direct the flow of the discussion in the way he intended, and he did so by tweaking the topic. "There's no need to overthink it. This planetoid has a vile temper, one that forces people to work together if they wish to survive. And our relations with the Samifjod go way back. This isn't just about us. The others need the Lifebone as well. We must return north, win this war, and save more people... Our only consideration is how we can secure the blessing." 
When the "north" was mentioned, the Sarkaz fell silent once more. Nobody knew how long this war was going to last, and they were already tired and sick of it. 
Curses. A mistake. 
Fleming wiped the sweat from his forehead. The best sales pitch should never, ever reveal its bottom line so quickly. While he squeezed out a smile and frantically prepared another topic to revive the discussion, a Vampiress sitting furthest away, one that Fleming hardly knew, whose name even escaped his memories, took the lead. Elegantly she leaned against her thorny spear of blood red carmine, and spoke in her gentle voice that Fleming was familiar with. 
"Why? Don't any of you look forward to this? Tell me how many Sarkazian cities did we have back on Terra?" she purred as moldable blood glistened and rippled in mid-air as it slowly took the form of a city. "And now we have this distant planet filled with mysteries. Imagine, if you can, the possibility of us forging an era of peace, and think of the Talosian land and skies — I believe the time has come for us to raise our new home." 
"A floating city that cruises through the heavens upon the bones of the Feranmut. It must have its own style, and a powerful name." Fleming heard himself talk. 
"What about New Kazdel? Wait, that sounds too big... How about New Furnace?" 
"It would need a ring of permanent artillery and defensive works. Don't want no flying buggerloids striking from the skies!" 
The discussion turned solemn, somber, and stern... The people's faces revealed their longing for the new city that they would soon be building with their hands. The hesitation and uncertainty that reigned over the emotions of the Sarkaz were dispelled, and an unprecedented urge of impatience took their places. While the crowd clamored and argued, someone blurted out the word — "Seš'qa". A word without the prestige or greatness most envisioned, a place to serve a simple purpose. A midway stopping point between the road forward and the road home. 
But it was a beautiful word. Fleming juggled it on his tongue and mulled over the delicate tremors felt by his lower mandible, given force by the pulmonary exhalation required to lend voice to the word. An idea slowly crept into his mind — Why should the Sarkaz be a dark, brooding people with a penchant for violence and seek only warfare as their companion? No. The new city should be a theme park with a giant wheel ride, open-air bazaar, theaters, and every element of fun that could fit, and it did not matter if the element was not part of the Sarkazian past. 
The northern winds cut like razors, and it was the frigid cold that kept Fleming's mind in a state of crystalline clarity. His imaginations went wild. He had events in mind. "Lift-Off Day", "Open Day", "Parade of the Royal Courts" — festivals that the Sarkaz could use to gently land upon this planet, like a dandelion seed. 
This new city would not be blanketed in smoke from the funeral pyres for the fallen warriors. Instead, it would have something far more beautiful, like fireworks to bless its existence. 
It did not matter what the others thought. The Speaker on the other side of the Cosmic Gate should love this idea. She would be happy whenever someone mentions anything about explosives. 
Fleming would have many chances to prove his skills as a merchant. The next course of action would be to sell this idea.

Before, reflecting on the past used to come naturally for Shiba Momiji. Back in school, she had a knack for breaking down a year's worth of progress with neat charts and detailed annotations — earning top grades with ease. 
But now, things are different. It's been a full year since Operations Team Z7 was formed. And instead of stats and milestones, what fills her heart now ... are feelings. 
She constantly worries about Catcher. As the team's shield and support, he looks after everyone like family. Is he overextending himself...? 
She pays attention to Estella's condition. Some may see her as unmotivated or laid-back, but Akekuri knows better. Estella is healing her own fragile body while quietly helping Op Z7 heal the world. That takes a rare kind of strength. 
She watches over Fluorite's moods, not just her frequent outbursts or headstrong ways. Akekuri often asks herself: Am I being a strong enough cushion? One that lets her feel understood and safe? 
She worries about Antal too. Often labeled an "odd one," Antal is, in truth, passionate and reliable — his way of connecting simply different. She sees how hard he's been working to keep pace with the team. 
It's because of them that Z7 stands as it does today. 
She's deeply grateful — for their trust, for their belief in her leadership, and for proving that this team, once seen as inexperienced, could stand on its own. 
But most of all, she wonders about herself: Has she met the expectations she set — using what little they had to help as many as possible ... and to find her own light in the process? 
Sometimes she wonders: if the ideals of Endfield are ever fulfilled, and peace finally comes — maybe, just maybe, her parents might reconcile. And perhaps she could go home, just like when she was little ... and share one peaceful family meal together again. 
She is giving her all to make that future possible. 

Annual Performance Report
SUBMITTED BY: Akekuri, Captain, Operations Team Z7 

Dear Supervisor Perlica, 
This report outlines the major operations and achievements of Operations Team Z7 over the past year. 
We completed 40 missions with a 95% success rate and zero casualties. These included 16 cross-region supply runs, 9 joint wildlands recon operations, 7 high-risk engineering escorts, and 8 emergency rescues. 
We've steadily grown from a provisional support force into a reliable, fully operational unit. 
P.S. While our combat rating remains average in this year's assessment, we ranked among the top in support, command, and management. 
......
Regarding the rumored awakening of the "Endministrator," though I have yet to witness it myself, I can feel the excitement in  stories shared by our seniors. If possible, I'd like to respectfully request that Operations Team Z7 be involved in missions under the Endministrator's command. It would be a privilege to personally deliver our tactical reports — and even more meaningful to work alongside the Endministrator to bring Endfield's vision to life. Together, we can restore peace to Talos-II...

Regular Work Report for Operators Under the Endministrator 
REPORTED BY: Laevatain 

I escorted the messenger to this volcanic basin. Molten lava flowed through the ground beneath our feet, heating the rain and creek, causing the earth to froth and bubble endlessly. The monitoring station stood right atop this "cauldron of living soup". 
This place is extremely poor in Originium. Resident scientists rely on geothermal heat to cook food. A ration tin can be cooked through simply by burying it in the dirt for an hour. They even have "pocket stews": a liquid stock and other ingredients sealed in a food-grade bag — after quick cooking, you can just tear it open with your teeth. I got a face full of hot stew once, and it felt like I was on fire. 
When I had my first meal, the scientist taught me to sing their "ritual" chant: "May your soup never spill, and may your flame never die." 
I sang the chant with him. It was the first time I received a stranger's blessing on Talos-II. 
— Sent from Monitoring Station 34 

As the Operator closest to the incident and the most capable emergency responder, I was ordered to reach the UWST base not marked on the map with the greatest speed I could muster. 
The issue was not complicated. Just an unexpected blast furnace malfunction, shutdown, and loss of power. I spent a bit of my powers and helped them re-ignite the core. Temperature returned to operational levels and the system was restored. The crisis was temporarily averted. 
Their "names" left quite an impression on me. The place was a secret base in the frigid lands of █████, usually referred to by its unique beacon code. Everyone there was forbidden from using their real names or any self-chosen codenames; only the "assigned" name was allowed. 
My temporary name here was "Olga Randall". I was told there were three others before me with the same name, and it's likely that the next replacement actuary sent here will also take on this name. 
It was a strange experience. I was just a temporary user of the name "Olga Randall". It felt similar to the memory fragments swimming in my mind. Neither the name nor the fragments were truly mine, but at that very moment, they were all part of me. 
— Sent from UWST Beacon DAU.14 

After eliminating the Aggelos camping in the freight station, I reopened the gate that had kept the tunnel sealed for quite a while. 
They maintained a low gravity environment within the tunnels. Refugees, trapped here for months, floated their way to the exit, trembling and struggling as they left the place. They must relearn how to walk and run under the ponderous influence of gravity. 
But there was a little girl who floated within the tunnels and danced for a bit before leaving the place. She told me it was how she kept herself calm and sane when they were trapped in this place. 
I memorized her dance, a comforting yet powerful routine of rhythms. If you want, I can show it to you and let you have a go once I head back. The moves aren't hard. It's all about the breathing and the rhythms. 
— Sent from freight nexus MC-20 

I've made plenty of new memories during this time. I still remember that you're chasing after your own memories as well. I found a few places related to the old "you". Seek me out if you're interested. 
— Emergency message, sent from Contact Point 084A

I remember our last encounter with the "Angel". It was one hundred days ago. It was February. It was our last sweep for potential cave-ins caused by Ankhorfalls. The Aggelos appeared without warning at the back of the team just as we approached the edge of a sinkhole. Old Liu was the first to get hit. His alarm failed to alert him and only started shrieking when the enemy disabled his Tianshi apparatus. That was how we learned of the threat. Tobin reacted quickly. He immediately fired at the Aggelos's abdomen. It howled and then swung its razor-sharp tail. Tobin and Kachinsky could not evade but took the hit for me. They bought me an opportunity to unload my last bullet. The Aggelos collapsed in pain. Maybe. People say the Aggeloi do not feel anything. Not even pain — This blightery is unfair. 
I never saw the Aggelos again after that. 
The war finally ended. 

The investiture was held at our base near the North. They organized it to praise and award the soldiers who performed admirably. As the only survival of Outpost 158, I walked in the middle of the column of awardees, flanked front, back, left, and right by veterans like me. We're all war heroes now, dressed in brand new uniforms fitting for the investiture. Speaking of uniforms, the last time I got a new outfit was during my first arrival at Talos-II. The local committee of the frontiers organized a mass marriage to uphold the spirit of the Black Hole Protocol. Fifty-two pairs of newlyweds from Yan, Ursus, Victoria ... settling down and starting families in this foreign world. I was one of them. I was young but crossing that Gate drained every ounce of courage out of me. Old Liu was young too. Just passed the Tianshi admission exams and so proud of himself. He took my hand and told me to have no fear. Liu promised that we would, together, overcome every obstacle of this world and build our new home upon this planet. 
And so I marched alone down the lengthy path towards the investiture platform. The cheering of the crowd was passionate, but distant. I counted the awardees and could not even finish. 
The war finally ended. 

The aftermath of the war was worse than we thought. Refugees from the north kept coming in. They brought news that "everything we built was gone". Every receiving area was packed of them. Sprawling industrial parks and factory plants from more than ten years ago are now replaced by drab, ashen temporary shelters. Riots quickly followed. Workers fought corporate soldiers in Development Zone 2. They were one step away from full out war. News of such unrest also fanned the unrest within the Tianshi Bureau. Some Tianshi started labeling factions as "Protocolites" and "Anti-Protocolites" and seemed eager to introduce hostilities amidst our ranks. Tianshi Ruan, one of Old Liu's classmate, petitioned the Bureau multiple times, hoping that they would issue an official statement to quell the increasingly antagonistic atmosphere. All he received was the same rebuke: "True strength lies in maintaining our unwavering neutrality." Some even tried to contact Dijiang that continued to cruise in orbit, but even Endfield Industries stayed silent. Only the attack on Hongshan-1 Mass Driver made them realize that the facade of neutrality can no longer disguise the long festering rifts amongst ourselves. 
It just another day, but a group of farmers barged into the Hongshan-1 power supply facilities. Though quickly apprehended and confined by the Tianshi, the farmers barked loudly at us: "Why won't you fix that Cosmic Gate! Why won't you send us home with this mass driver?" The Tianshi paid them no heed and kept them behind bars. One of the arrested farmers was a Feline girl less than ten years of age. She asked her father: "Papa, why are we going home? I thought we have a home at this place." Her father could not give her an answer. 
Then again, how are we supposed to tell her that this massive "refugee camp" was her home? How are we supposed to explain why we left Terra and stepped onto this planet in the first place? Many of us could hardly remember the reasons. 
We found ourselves trapped behind a prison of our own making. 
The war finally ended. 

There was a minor disturbance during noon. It was deliberately started it to distract the patrolling Tianshi. We came out of hiding from the vehicles and crossed the boundary line. A young security Tianshi guarded the final pass out of Hongshan. Our gazes crossed as I loaded a round into the firing chamber. The Tianshi did not activate his alarm or raise his Arts Unit. 
"I'm a humble disciple of Tianshi Ruan, and I've been waiting for a while," his words brought me out of my startled stupor. 
"What of Tianshi Ruan himself?" 
"My mentor instructed that the departure is best done in groups. He left before any of you. If finding a new home is your wish, he will do his best to see it fulfilled." 
He pushed a pass of emerald bamboo into my hand as he spoke. "Qingbo" was the word inscribed upon it. 
"Exit the city, then make for the mountains. He shall meet you there." 
The war finally ended.

No matter where you run into Supervisor Perlica aboard the Dijiang, she always calmly greets you before immediately returning to her work. Some even joke that beneath her Liberi appearance, she might actually be a machine, perfectly executing the directives of some higher intelligence. While this kind of rumor spreads widely among newer operators, the Supervisor does not mind it at all. In fact, she occasionally plays along with the joke on purpose, lightening the mood and helping to ease the tension among the crew. 
According to the unofficial account by Martin Marvin Malen, after officially assuming the role of Supervisor, Perlica forced herself to adopt the most appropriate demeanor to fulfill her duties. But accumulated emotions and pressure always need an outlet. Even before the Endministrator's return, Perlica had already found a way to truly relax. "Have you heard of the 'Crankcase Creative Contest'? They say it originally started as a creative showdown between a certain Vampire genius and a mysterious mechanic. Seniors in the R&D Center brought this ancient Terra event to Endfield. Nowadays, the wild ideas that emerge from the CCC not only bring a lot of laughter to the operators, but also greatly drive our technological innovation. Yet very few know that the true force behind this event at Endfield is Supervisor Perlica. After all, she has never officially participated, and rarely voices her opinions. In truth, her reason for reviving this event was simply to create a platform where she could relieve her restless hands and test the strange ideas in her head." 

Even though I was banned from competing this year, I wouldn't call myself entirely absent. After all, I’m the one who named the award-winning "Blast-ma Roar"! When its creator came to me with the idea of "stuffing a gravity firearm into an acceleration engine", I knew it had potential. We ended up taking apart quite a few fine firearms to make it work, though… Huh? O-of course we didn't touch my dad's precious stockpile! 
—The reigning champion of multiple Crankcase Creative Contests, a prodigy in firearm engineering.

-1284744833070049894:
In a time when most Landbreakers are seen as "destroyers of order", the Pack stands out as an anomaly. They value order and hold a peaceful attitude toward the Civilization Band. Even now, they cling to certain old traditions, such as strong familial bonds and a deep respect for unity. 
That very difference only fueled the long-standing feud between them and their rivals, the Bonekrushers. Over ten years ago, the Bonekrushers struck with a vicious ambush, shattering the Pack when they were at their weakest — just after the death of their Alpharion. 
Wulfgard and his younger sister survived the attack, but they refused to speak of what truly happened. 
Wulfgard then left the Pack a few years after his coming-of-age ceremony, keeping in touch with only a few trusted friends and his sister. 
No one ever knew why he left. He stayed silent, just like he did about the attack. 
Later, he approached Endfield and proposed a partnership. He eventually joined the Specialist Tech Division as an operator. 
Someone once asked why he chose Endfield. 
At first, he was silent. Then, with startling honesty, he answered: 
"I want another future for the Pack... and Endfield holds the possibility of making it real." 
Wulfgard spoke candidly of the Pack's struggles. His steady resolve and honest intent opened doors. 
So it made perfect sense when he became an operator. As he put it, he had a duty — to prove the Pack's worth and to repay Endfield's trust in him. 
Since then, he's become a quiet but reliable presence on many tough and dangerous missions. 
Operators who once held deep prejudice against the Landbreakers began to change their views — thanks to Wulfgard. 
Then, opinions shifted once more after the arrival of his sister — Operator Rossi. But that's a story for another time...

What do I think of the north? Worst place ever ... I swear! I seriously messed up agreeing to join Rooter on his hunt for that mysterious Sami vendor out in the middle of nowhere! We went over the first snowpeak and were barely two days into the north when some Blighted snowstorm "caught" us at the foot of the mountains! 
I will never forget the sight of an entire burdenbeast being swooshed away by the Blight-tainted snow. The only thing on my mind was: "Blasted blightery! I'm gonna die here..." 
But I guess I saved up enough luck for the past decade or so! The snowstorm was just meters away from us when an Ursus girl swooped in from the skies — I kid you not! She flew in on a snowboard, pulled off a perfect landing next to us, slammed a shield on the ground, and suddenly a wall of ice appeared with a WOOSH! That wall kept the snowstorm away! 
Anyway, she saved both Rooter and me. She escorted us into a cave that she called our temporary shelter. 
And there were all sorts of people there... Oathkeepers, Seš'qa caravan drivers, and even Landbreakers! 
I still remember how we just walked in and some tall and mean-looking Feline started pointing his finger at us, "These two! They're frauds plotting to bring their swindling ways to Sami! I heard all about their dirty plots along the way. Why are you saving these lowlives? Don't let them cheat you!" It was only then when I suddenly recognized the Feline. He was the guide who traveled with us a few days back... I had wondered why he suddenly returned the commission and refused to guide us any longer... 
Anyway, I thought we were finished but the Ursus lass who brought us in said nothing. She gave the Feline a glance and the big mean kittyboy ... just sat down and said nothing else. 
I wanted to thank her personally back then, but she soon rushed out to carry on with her SAR. I couldn't even get her name. Another SAR team soon arrived and brought us to safety. 
But I recognized the badges and markings on her outfit. They were the same as the illustrations in the shelter. 
What happened next...? Well, I found your place. That's what happened. Hah! Just take these supplies. My token of gratitude to that Ursus lass! 
— Recordings from a donor of the Northern Corridor Rescue Union

I happen to have personal experience in the practice and field use of the spear. Here are my two cents. All 3 versions published by TGCC are fake, and contain plenty of ridiculous and misleading errors. Every version of the Martial Codex includes records of Yanese spearmancy such as Spear of Empyrean Return and Pear Blossom Spear of Wuling. But one of the versions made a super exaggerated claim that ancient Tianshi could flick the sun and moon with their spears. They even furnished this section with great warriors of questionable authenticity flying all over the place (for details, refer to the Wrankwood movie industry during the Age of Terra, plenty of their stuff is based on false fantasies). The Martial Codex we have in the EFDB might be a dry and boring read, but it contains detailed records and identities of the practitioners and masters of various spearmancy schools. The Codex even has commentaries and suggestions written by the practitioners themselves. The Codex has detailed descriptions of everything from folk martial artists to Imperial Guards of Yan, Silverlance Pegasi of Kazimierz, wielders of Victorian piledriver spears, and even Kazdelian mercenaries. The author is truly admirable for being able to secure such a huge range of resources while giving off the vibe of being on equal standing of numerous legends! The commentaries were also written in a concise yet vivid style. It takes great conviction to achieve this. Hence, I truly believe that the Martial Codex in the EFDB is the original from the Age of Terra. The others that we can easily buy are just crude and exaggerated copies. A true shame, if you ask me.

Antal was born in a normal household in the Free City of New Wrankwood. He spent most of his childhood growing up in a household Originium appliance repair shop belonging to his grandmother. 
Although Antal lived in a place known for its entertainment industry, he had no interest in the movies or performance industries. Instead, he preferred lying on the table and looking at his grandmother work — Her jobs include repairing a faulty refrigerator and swapping out its Originium starter component, or restoring a television with a shattered screen and severely damaged mainboard to mint conditions... The old repairlady had jobs everyday, but she never neglected her grandson. When she had time, she would personally design and make various toys such as mini sports cars and powered combo-puzzle cubes for the lad. Hence, Antal grew up very much loved and never felt lonely. Years of influence from his grandmother gave Antal an outstanding talent for assembling and taking apart Originium devices. He successfully secured a full scholarship in an academy and chose a major related to applications of Originium automation. 
The academy where Antal studied at was known for its conservative atmosphere. The youth, however, was not an adherent to the rules. When his novel inventions failed to acquire the favor of his professors, he chose to continue his project in private. For his academic excellence, Antal became the valedictorian for the graduation ceremony. He mounted his latest invention on his back — an automated Originium-powered robot arm, and enthusiastically used it to wave at the professors who once scoffed at the idea. And then suddenly, the open hand of the robot lowered four of its fingers, save for one that remained still and fully extended. 
Although the incident left quite a psychological trauma to members of the academy's administration, Antal was still able to graduate. However, no one in the academy was willing to offer letters of recommendation to his potential employers. Endfield Industries initiated a talent recruitment drive in cities near New Wrankwood a while later. The advanced technologies and pioneering spirit of the company seized Antal by his heart. He then submitted his resume to Endfield. After the interview, Antal was chosen by Operator Akekuri who was setting up an operations team of her own. He later became a formal member of Operations Team Z7.

5781618409543038911:
I once had extreme confidence.
Confidence for my gifts in wielding the (applicable) Originium Arts. And my gifts were rare indeed, even when taking every caster of Talos-II into account.
I believe all of my Arts instructors I had since my childhood could attest to this fact, and there were 23 of them.
While my peers struggled to light a candle with an Arts Unit, I was debating the possibility of having an unaided Infected cast the Arts for extended periods time and at higher throughputs... It was a time when I first heard about the legendary Endministrator. Back then, at least, I once believed that I might be capable of achieving the same.
My performances in the Originium Arts Proficiency Assessment for the last 20 years, my GPA from the courses on Originium Arts theories during the academy, and the accolades I received for my graduation thesis titled The Gap Between Practical Applications and Theory — A Discourse on the Future of the Originium Arts, only served to strengthen my belief as I spent every year perfecting my Arts. There is a significant possibility that I am a "genius".
— And I held on to that belief until I joined the company that I have dreamed about since my childhood. Endfield Industries.

I could hardly describe my feelings when I underwent the routine integrated physical examinations for new employees and received the report.
— My Originium Arts Assimilation was rated as "Standard". How was it possible? They must have made a mistake.
At that moment, I felt as though I was struck by the devious Arts of a Djall, and it struck so hard I could fight off the mental fog.
When I came to my senses, I went straight to the Human Resources Division and delivered a severe protest. I demanded a re-examination and declared my absolute refusal to accept such a brusque conclusion made without sufficient evidence.
The HR Division seemed to be expecting my applications. I was entreated by Martin Marvin Malen in a most sincere manner.
"...We understand your requests and have arranged two additional Originium Arts Assimilation testing sessions after three working days. A total of two operators will also be assigned to take the tests with you and serve as control references."

Three days later —
As per the instructions, I cut out a perfect square out of a ferric slab before me with my Arts Unit. I turned around saw the Savra who should be at the opposing testing station. He looked at me curiously.
"Is this the way to do it? I thought I had to cut 16 squares with a single move!"
This is my confession. I thought I heard him wrongly and subconsciously gazed at the results of his test... And I saw sixteen perfect squares neatly laid out on the floor of the training cabin. The clock stopped at exactly 1 minute and 1 second.
— What was I doing at that time? Oh, I just finished calibrating my Arts Unit and thought about the perfect approach to start cutting the slab.

There was no question that I lost the first trial. It was a complete disaster.
But negativity had yet to catch up to me. I simply prepped for the second session. I comforted myself with this thought: "Endfield's a big place, and they have a legend like the Endministrator. A fellow Endfielder of such competence ... should be something to expect."
Soon, an accident, or the stroke of Fate ... dawned upon me.
While I was checking the Arts Unit, an Ægir youth wearing an elite operator's uniform poked his head out of the training cabin. He simply wagged his tail and undid the safeties of over fifty standard Arts Units. They orbited him like an obedient school of fins as he left the place and mumbled these words: "What a hassle... Shouldn't have come here at the first place..."
This was when I first experienced despair from seeing an "unattainable gap" that could never be closed.
I learned that even if I mastered every form of Originium Arts to my knowledge, the tracelessness and effortless elegance of his Arts wielding were qualities that I could never achieve...
Never, not in my entire lifetime.
I suddenly felt that all my achievements in the Arts for the last twenty years only gave me better knowledge of what I witnessed at a particular moment in life — I am not the prodigy. That title belongs to someone else.
I chose to forfeit the second testing session.

After the test, I also gave up joining the Specialist Tech Division. Thankfully, the Arsenal took a good look at my CV and asked if I was interested in doing some weapon engineering.
I agreed.

They said that the classic "Arts Identifier" would be returning for the Arts Unit Obstacle Challenge this year — I received five of those, but I would not mind getting a sixth.

"..." 
"You're right. It's never too late...!"

Wulfgard knew better than anyone, that leaving the Pack for good meant this journey had no return date. By his own standards, that meant packing everything that might prove useful. 
Yet, standing before Il Cacciatore and sweeping his gaze over the massive rig that had been his and his sister's home for nearly a decade... he realized, abruptly, that there was nothing left worth taking. 
He went over his plans once more in his mind: make sure Rossi knew exactly who in the clan could be trusted, confirm the two ways people could reach him, ask Tommaso to keep a close watch over Rossi, settle the last bit of custom work fees at Uncle Rust's, feed Giovanni's semi-wild fowlbeasts one last time, entrust them to little Vincenzo next door... No, he hasn't forgotten a thing. 
Satisfied, he turned for one final check. Just to be absolutely sure he hadn’t left Rossi's handmade Originium lamp glowing on the bedside table. 
But as soon as he stepped into his sleeping compartment, his eyes caught sight of something in an unremarkable corner of the cabinet: his worn guns — the very first weapons he'd ever owned. 
Though secondhand and now running low on compatible ammo, those guns were priceless treasures back then. They kept him and his sister alive, earned him his first mercenary contract, and helped him take down his first target. When one of the Originium activators failed, he was forced to master one-handed reloads and gun maintenance. After three years of supporting his family with mercenary pay, he finally replaced the worn Originium activator and even crafted a set of custom-etched ammo. 
These guns were passed down from the clan's elders. Like many inherited dreams, they met their end during a high-stakes escort mission, overheating after prolonged firing. 
Soon after, Uncle Rust — a bounty hunter who had returned to the Pack and opened a weapon refurbishment shop called "Howlfire Gunsmiths." There, Wulfgard was introduced to custom weapon modifications for the first time. 
Then he learned to make weapons truly his own, even if they only suited him. 
Still, he never got rid of those guns that got him started. They remained tucked away in a quiet corner. 
Why keep them? As a reminder? A keepsake? Or a memento of painful memories? 
He wasn't sure — maybe all, maybe none. 
After confirming the Originium lamp was off, he headed for the door, ready to embark on a journey that might finally give him an answer.

At first I be like, man, I was going straight to hell! But later I got a job at town, roof and bed, plus nice food. Then I learned that Mad Mimi be giving us options. She got that mean face and talked like I owed her money, but Mimi probably had to go plow through tons of burdo-shite trying to get some of the Fam decent gigs. 
Oh yeah, you heard, the loot stashes at the grove that we've been nicking from the Wulingers are actually extra supplies from town. I was a bit confused why bother carry the old and obsolete tools to that place. Turned out they were meant for the Stockade. People say Mad Mimi is super tough on the Stockade Fam, but actually she's always helping and caring in her sneaky way. 
— Anonymous, current citizen of Wuling (former Qingbo Stockade resident)

With a flutter of crimson, she touched down bearing saccharine candies, animal-shaped origami, and a kaleidoscope of colored pencils. 
The kids swarmed around the mysterious Miss Messenger, who came by every now and then with treats, gifts, and tales they'd never heard before. 
Together, they drew her stories' vibrant fowlbeasts, then folded sugary foil into tiny mirrors of themselves. 
As the evening bell rang, she said goodbye to each kid, watching them run home. 
One girl tugged softly at Miss Messenger's skirt. She had nowhere to go. 
With a gentle touch to her head, the Messenger sent the girl floating upward as a startled yelp escaped her lips. 
Together, they watched the moon climb the night sky as stars arranged themselves into fleeting constellations. 
"Miss ... aren't you going home?" 
The girl whispered, lowering her head, knowing the Messenger would soon leave her. 
"My home... lies beyond the far horizons. Or should I say, it hides beyond the sky and behind the stars themselves." 
"Behind the stars?" 
"Would you like to visit?" 
The girl nodded, then shook her head. She ached to go, yet feared troubling her beloved Miss Messenger. 
"Don't worry. I've told my colleagues about a brilliant little girl. They all want to meet you too." 
"R-really?" 
"Uh-huh. I would never lie to you. Oh, wait, it's time." 
"It's ... time?" 
"Close your eyes and don't peek. In three ... two ... one ... Voila!" 
In Miss Messenger's hands appeared two cupcakes. 
"Woah..." 
"Hehe, today's your birthday, right? Of course I remembered! This one's just for you." 
The girl stared wide-eyed at the Messenger as she dipped her cream-coated finger into her mouth, beaming with a sweet smile. 
"I- I want to visit your home..." 
To her, this cupcake was a treasure beyond price, held carefully as fragile glass.
Now aboard the Dijiang, she studies tirelessly to become an official technician at the EF-ED. 
Whenever challenges arise, she takes a cupcake to the Bridge and gazes toward Talos-II. She finds herself drawing courage from that familiar crimson figure, always trailing a scent of sugar and resolve.

Ahem. Hello people. I'm the new candidate consultant for angling strategies and instructor for hobby angling... Never heard of it? Ah. Yeah, I think some boss man prolly misread my resume and decided to hire me. Maybe he sneezed and got me approved. I'm just an angler and fin seller, you know. It's also possible that your Endfield system got too many loopholes, since a freezer can get treated as frontline combat hardware. Anyway, I got in. 
Okay. Since no one is shooing me away, I'll try to share my true knowledge. It's not going to be engineering or tactics. I'm talking about Angling. Don't underestimate Angling. It's outdoor meditation for true anglers. Those who don't know anything call it old boy's excuse to be lazy. I'll tell you about angling with the Endfield lingo. It is a miniaturization of a tactical operation. You got a bait, a hook, deception, and patience. So, who ends up slipping? Who gets hooked? Who becomes bait? And who enjoys deep fried fins on the shore? It's all about luck and vision. 
Now let's take a look at two basic terms — float angling and bottom angling. 
What is float angling? It's just scattering the bait in the water and looking at your float. You may think you caught something when the float moves a little. But when you lift your rod with excitement, you realize the fin never bit, and is in fact "laughing" and blowing bubbles at you. Some fins just take two bites and swim away. And some don't even like the bait. They just snag the line a bit and take you for a fool. It's like a turf battle. The bandit gives a funny look and you think he's about to make a move... But turns out he only remembered that he forgot about the spices for the fin stew. Angling is not about mysterious techniques. It's all about not snapping your rod after twelve missed pulls. 
So what is bottom angling? You dig a hole for yourself and then sink a bait. And then ... nothing else happens. The fins just ignore what you did. Maybe they'll roll their eyes before moving on. I used to know a gang advisor who is an expert in bottom angling. He always says: "Stop moving, son. They fear you more if you stay still." So, Senhor Advisor would spend all day on his second-hand rocking chair while they break our legs out there. And then he would squint his eyes and go: "Look. The enemy has taken the bait." — Take the friggin' bait. I hope the old bastard shits rocks and dies. I was the friggin' bait. 
Got a little carried away. Anyway, angling is a great sport. Just start angling if you wanna know how fun it is! In my humble opinion, it is far healthier than sitting here looking into the cold, dark space... So your question is, why am I even here? 
Decent canteen food and no one's clocking my naps. Pretty nice place, actually. 
 — Alesh's contribution to the Hobby-Sharing Get Together

...Let me get this straight. Your team lost to Z7 in the combat drill 'cause you didn't graduate from a military school and Lil' Dodge wasn't your instructor?
Enough excuses, kid. I trained tons of raw recruits like you and I totally lost count on the number of losers who hamstring themselves by boo-hooing about their sad backstories.
Look at your face! Do you think I'm gonna give you a motivational story how a missing degree or diploma isn't that important? HAH! WRONG! I'm your friggin' instructor, not your pathetic shrink! I'm not going to make you feel good about your academic failures!
Since we mentioned degrees, then I gotta say — it's actually pretty important.
But if you're missing one, there are solutions to go about it.

I became an instructor after all. Guess how I did it?
WRONG AGAIN! I, Sato Kogo, never read a proper book in my life. In fact, I only learned how to write in Victorian thanks to courses offered aboard Dijiang. When I was your age, I was just a bummed out debt collector in Neo Tsukushi!
Wha? Don't you know what a debt collector is...? Ugh. Forget it. I'll put it simply. Hired muscle. That was my job.
So did that for about three or four years. I was either bruising people or getting bruised myself. As long as someone paid the creds, it didn't really matter to me.

I was in my twenties and I thought I'd be doing that for the rest of my life... I never expected something big to happen.
Oh yes... Stepped on a few toes. The wrong tail, actually. Not some cartel security firm, but an actual big shot oyabun.
Ugh. This is exactly why I kept telling you to pay attention to the surroundings when you fight. I learned it the very hard way, so at least take this from me.

Weather was great that day. I besieged that gambling den with two dozen bros from the organization. There were just around eight people on the other side and I thought it would be a cakewalk.
But those dudes fought like beasts in heat. Half of the lads were down in a heartbeat. I was out of ideas but I couldn't just leave my bros behind. So I came up with the clever idea of using the revolving doors...
How did I do it? Well, i simply undid the security latch and got it spinning... Anyways, I got two enemies down in an instant. Some of the bros started helping and we sent the rest of them packing.
There was one thing I miscalculated. The revolving door was connected to the one upstairs. Now that wouldn't sound like a thing but my boss suddenly got the bright idea of enjoying the spectacle. Suffice to say, his tail got caught — Boss man was also a Lupo and you know what they do when somebody messes with their tail.
What happened next? Geesh. Do I have to spell it out? I escaped to the frontiers before they gave me cement shoes! I slogged two years in trucking, four in janitorial work, and three in bounty hunting. My liver was dying on me and luck finally turned when I arrived at Endfield — Some old client wrote me a recommendation. Thank the Big Gas for that.

Alright. Your turn. Tell me about your plans on beating Z7 next time?

War Song of the Samifjod
Sun melts the snow,
Under the frozen earth, shadows flee. 
But our wandering does not end. 
Sun splits the clouds, 
In the forest, rain departs. 
But our warfare does not stop. 
Lift shields, don plates, 
Fate holds us here. 
Under the sun, 
We bleed and fight.

After arriving on Talos-II from Terra, the Feranmut Sami ended His years-long drift and chose a plot of land within the polar circle, settling there along with the Myrkwood He carried on His back. Under the Feranmut's protection, the Sami people enjoyed a brief period of peace. But soon, with the destruction of the Cosmic Gate and the outbreak of the First Aggeloi War, the Feranmut Sami gave His life to protect the Sami people, falling in the North Pole. The Sami people barely had time to mourn before they had to join in the construction of the Oathkeepers' fortress. What followed was a long campaign that has continued to this very day.
When Typhoeus awoke on Rhodes Island and learned of her people's current mission, she immediately packed her bags and headed north. But after traveling a great distance to the Oathkeeper's fortress, a Sami Snowpriest just back from the battlefield gave her a pat on the back of the head, a slap reeking of earth, and turned her away at the door.
"Come back when you are taller than your bow, then you can go to war."
Though Typhoeus insisted that she was simply petite, no one believed her. After all, her hands had yet to develop the thick calluses that came from years of drawing a bow.
Lost and dejected, she could only board a wagon bound for Myrkwood to meet the kin she had never known. This was the Sami she remembered, the environment, the customs, the language, the accents, all preserved. Yet at the same time, it all felt foreign to her. In the settlement, there were only the elderly, the wounded, and the children. Those who could still bear arms had all chosen to head to the front lines, guarding that line forged of flesh and blood, holding back the Aggeloi's march southward.
Typhoeus, lost and adrift, remained in Myrkwood. She soon learned that after the fall of Sami, His legends had also been shattered. The elders who knew the old tales had turned to bone on the battlefield alongside Sami himself before they could pass the stories on. So Typhoeus, unable to fight on the front lines, decided to gather those legends and preserve them.

Endmin, did you know? The fall of Sami was Sami's own choice. The people accepted Him and followed without hesitation.
I found a Foldartal used for divination in Myrkwood. On it was recorded a "communication" between the Snowpriest and Sami.
Before He descended upon the north, He had warned the people of Myrkwood that He had long foreseen a cruel and protracted war. He would have to go north and, at some future moment, sacrifice Himself to protect all living things.
He gave His people the chance to leave...
But on the Foldartal were the people's response—
The will of Sami is the will of the Sami people. The mission of Sami is the mission of the Sami people. We will go north with you.
The hunt never ends.

DOCUMENT: HR Promotion Records of Wuling Scientific Developmental District 
NAME: Mi Fu 
REGION OF ORIGIN: Wuling 
WORK EXPERIENCE: 3 years 
CURRENT POSITION: Wuling Watchguard 
PROPOSED PROMOTION: Wuling Watchguard Captain 

CURRICULUM VITAE & BACKGROUND: 
Mi Fu was a Qingbo Stockade resident who was later recruited by the Wuling Scientific Developmental District, and was made a watchguard after the completion of Wuling City. Since assuming the role, she has constantly worked at the frontlines, demonstrating extensive knowledge regarding security issues within Wuling City and the peripheral regions, as well as decisiveness and alacrity when handling various emergencies and cases. Mi Fu is committed to Wuling City, has zero tolerance for any form of delinquency or criminality, and always acts with strict justice. She has a good reputation, exercises effective deterrence, and serves as a rallying point for the general public. 

STRENGTHS: 
Exceptional combat prowess. Impressive physicals and fortitude. Capable of handling high-risk threats. 
Decisive and skilled in executing orders. Capable of making the right calls when facing complex situations. 
Caring and nurturing towards those working under her. Capable of forming a strong, cohesive team. 
Good reputation among the general populace and has earned their trust and support. Public reviews include: "A little blunt but always just." 

AREAS TO IMPROVE ON: 
Over eagerness in applying force. Tendency to employ physical measures when resolving various situations. Lack of procedural awareness. 
Slight disadvantage in clerical work such as report drafting. Limited administrative skills. 
Quick tempered. Lacks patience for communication. Prone to conflicts with others. 
Gives inordinate trust to familiar individuals. Decision-making may be affected by personal relationships and emotions. 

OVERALL RATING: 
Mi Fu has delivered remarkable results in patrol work and law enforcement. Having successfully quelled multiple emergencies, she is a promising officer who can be relied upon for field work. However, she inclines toward blunt approaches that lack finesse, has poor procedural awareness, and runs the risk of violating the proper chain of command. Nevertheless, the general public is very satisfied with Mi Fu's performance. The candidate has made positive contributions, although mistakes are not absent. Further guidance and strengthening of her self-restraint will be required. 

OPINIONS OF THE REVIEWER(S): 
Mi Fu has a fiery disposition and a great passion for upholding justice. Though she often acts out of turn, her actions are never meant for ill. She swings her fists not for herself, but for the safety of the people. Callousness is a mere outcome of her straightforwardness. Occasions of procedural non-compliance and lack of clerical perfection only hide, not cancel, her meticulous attention to detail. She may fall short in such areas, but they are also where she excels. 
I am willing to vouch for her character and good standing, and to recommend her for promotion to Watchguard Captain of Wuling City, where she will become the mainstay of the city's public safety. I will also personally supervise and guide Mi Fu in her daily work. 

REVIEWER(S): Zhuang Fangyi 
October 19, Year 145

Fuyao:
Mama dreamed of you last night again. By this time, you should be back at Baizao with your Dada and having fun together with your grandparents. The streets should be filled with the smells of delicious feasts for New Year's Eve. Had your dumplings yet? Hope your Dada didn't make them this time. He never learned how to make them proper — He never rested his dough properly, and his wrappings were either too thick or too thin. If he insisted, just pray he wouldn't mess up again. I remember that time when you were one year old. He hid a coin in the dumplings and you accidentally choked on it. Your entire face turned blue and I was panicking beyond words. Thankfully the old Tianshi visited us at just the right time and saved your life.
Alas, the mobile container-home where we once ate dumplings together got smashed by an Ankhor. Everything got drilled straight into the earth, including those crooked couplets. Mama is now escorting the crew of the pioneering base southwards. Thank goodness your father is now off duty so I got him to bring you home to the rest of the family... Otherwise you'd be on this terrible road with me, crying non-stop from the cold and hunger. The monstrosities they call "Aggeloi" are merciless and cruel. But don't you worry, your Mama's a master in the School of Thunder.
For tonight, we found shelter in a valley. A farmer lady made a new year rice cake soup with the food we had left and doled it out to everyone. Mama also snipped out a few window flowers and pasted them on our temporary shelter. There are workers singing a chorus with their coarse yet passionate Ursine and Victorian accents. Mama certainly did not expect to be separated from you and Dada for our second New Year Festival in Talos-II.
Mama misses you. And if you miss Mama, just squeeze the doll I tucked in your wrappings. Mama made it, you know. I can totally feel your tender squishes, no matter the number of stars that separate us.
Sincerely, Mama

Fuyao:
You're about to go to school, right? Mama wonders how tall you are right now. Who do you look like more? Mama or Dada? How goes your lessons? I'm sorry I couldn't be at your side and help you with your homework. Though your Dada graduated from the Academy, he could never figure out mathematics. I hope he doesn't slow you down. Speaking of which, what is your favorite subject right now?
So, do you know the origins of your name, Fuyao? Mama and Dada came to Talos-II because we love the cosmos. You were born right under the Cosmic Gate. We thought you might just become a Tianshi of spaceflight and thus named you Fuyao, the rapid essence. But names are just a dream. Mama's actual wish is to see you grow up in peace. I don't care if you like reading or enjoy doing other things. Mama will always support your choice.
Times are difficult in this war we are fighting. Not too long ago my mentor paid a visit and asked me to join a project on building a great vessel to orbit around Talos-II. We're not the only one. The team includes many Terrans stranded at this place... Everyone generously provided all the secret tech, artifacts, and wonders they have. Many of these are unique technological marvels that could never be recreated, but they willingly staked everything for the sake of victory.
Mama is now part of the project, but I'm just responsible for the design and construction of a small support module. I never thought I could reach for the stars with my own strength so quickly. Then again, Mama also felt I've been waiting for this moment for far too long.
After all, we've spent too many days suffering upon this planet, and I missed too many moments of you growing up.
Sincerely, Mama

Fuyao:
The war has ended. But I can't but feel bitter about what happened after our "victory". We could no longer return to Terra. Every road home has been permanently closed. We failed to make any progress. Not only that, we almost annihilated ourselves in the internecine conflicts that followed.
Mama dreamed of you again. I saw you all grown up and becoming an accomplished Tianshi with a Tianshi apparatus in hand. But when I woke, I realized I could hardly remember how you looked like in the dream. We haven't met for so many years. Do you still remember how Mama looked like? You probably won't recognize Mama right now since Mama's not that young anymore. Hongshan is a massive crater, and it has been granted to the Tianshi who stayed in Talos-II. There are many compatriots from Yan here. Together, we built the Hongshan Academy of Sciences and started growing crops at this place. Mama shared the techniques and knowledge of hydroponics that I prepared for the space-faring tech demo. It took us several years but we finally received a bountiful harvest. Plenty of people can finally stop worrying about starving when the next batch of seeds are ready.
Once our granaries are full and our people clothed, I hope we can once again cast our eyes upon the celestial heights. Though the Cosmic Gate is beyond our reach, Mama shall take a great ship, ride the uplifting Fuyao vortex, sail through the stars, and reunite with you.
Please wait for that day, my dearest darling child.
Sincerely, Mama

"Age can be a real bummer, old man. Your spearmancy ... got slow and clunky.“ 
The Kuranta thrust the spear into the cracked rooftop and removed the heavy armor pieces. 
"You're just a few years younger than me, so that makes you just as old. Don't tell me that you're still a brat in love with heroic tales." 
"Stop being stupid and head back with me. The warlord Jakub is dead. His dream of 'an even greater city' is no more. This isn't worth dying for." 

"I thought you'd see things my way." the Kuranta looked at the Liberi who stepped over the body of the thirty-ninth Landbreaker, then drew a short blade from a once-ornate scabbard covered in decades of rust. The blade itself glimmered coldly. "I believe in the dream, the one our mentor told us when we were handed these blades. Go back to Terra and let the Golden Age return again. But an Ankhor smashed his tomb. We even couldn't make our way back to the north of Talos-II... Jakub wasn't the only one disappointed. You treat us as dreamers. Tell me then, what is that utopia thing long promised by the Civilization Band when we're facing 'occasional' supply shortages, encroaching Blight masses, and Aggelos attacks?" 

The Liberi sighed with resignation, stopped ten paces away from the Kuranta, pressed a boot into the windswept dust, and made the roof creak. 
"You chose a good place. Strong winds on the roof. The fowlbeasts could easily soar without flapping their wings." 
"Strong winds indeed ... but they're dying down." the Kuranta raised the blade, "We won the Aggeloi War. But what happened next? We're getting old. I'll never live to see my mentor's dream if I kept waiting. I have to act." 
"That's no excuse for following Jakub and pointing our mentor's lance against those who have even less and suffer more." 
"The strong devours the weak. Someone had to do it." the Kuranta straightened and gave a few rather clumsy swings of the blade, "I chose this path to fulfill our mentor's dream... You can't stop me." 
"You were once a hero who charged for ten miles to save a village from an Aggelos attack," the Liberi drew a weapon. It was the exact same sword wielded by the Kuranta. 
He still remembered the day when their mentor handed the blades to them and how his eyes sparkled the moment his fingers touched the weapon. He remembered how his sworn brother asked for their mentor's lance, and how he laughed when his sworn brother boasted about becoming a "great hero". Why did he laugh? The reason escaped his memories. 

"Hero? I'm no hero," the Kuranta raised the blade to chest level, "The hero you mentioned only lives in your mind, or he probably died that night." 
"Your actions disgrace our mentor's lance." the Liberi's handcannon was out of etched ammo and he tossed it away before charging towards the Kuranta, "Return it." 
"See if you're good enough ... to take it off my hands."

After the Qingbo Stockade incident, we initially expected to receive a confused, grieving, or angry operator. In preparation, we had arranged some psychological intervention measures to help ease her trauma. Yet, when Tangtang arrived aboard the Dijiang via tele-protocol, her face was lit with a bright smile, not a shadow of distress in sight.
Supervisor Perlica reminded us that despite the complexity of her community, Tangtang managed to rally her scattered people with her own charisma. This proves she possesses a resilient spirit capable of bearing significant responsibility.
And indeed, Tangtang proved far more perceptive than we had imagined. Her awareness and sensitivity to situations are second to none. In planning the subsequent development of Qingbo Stockade, she consistently prioritized the welfare of its residents, skillfully ensuring that every individual, young, old, sick, or disabled, was accounted for with a blend of boldness and attentiveness, guaranteeing no one would be overlooked or forgotten amidst the busy tasks. This quality is particularly valuable to us: in work involving diverse cultural practices, having a guide who understands the complex local interpersonal dynamics and ecosystem saves us significant communication costs in our development efforts.
Tangtang has adapted to life aboard Dijiang remarkably quickly. At times, we see her walking alongside Chen Qianyu, the Endministrator, or Supervisor Perlica, her eyes sparkling, tail swaying gently. She's also made some new friends, giving them affectionate nicknames in the style of Qingbo Stockade. Moreover, everything about Dijiang seems to fascinate her, especially the canteen's vending machine... She circled it several times on her first day. An operator kindly stepped forward to show her how to insert coins and press the colored buttons to get a drink to roll out. She listened quietly, though it was hard to tell if she fully understood... That evening, the vending machine triggered an alarm, and Operator Xaihi ended up having to retrieve a stuck "Tangtang Cert" from the coin slot.
After several months of observation, our conclusion is that: not only does Tangtang not require psychological support from us, but her presence has, in fact, infused Dijiang with renewed vitality.
When we discussed this with operators familiar with her, Chen Qianyu remarked with a smile, "Though Tangtang grew up by the water, she's more like an unquenchable flame. A passing storm might dampen it, but that spark quickly reignites and burns bright again."
One afternoon, we overheard Tangtang chatting with someone, her tone as candid as ever: "The Chief's head isn't that big, kiddo. I can't keep trying to figure things out, you know. It'll just make me dumb!"
