"I guess we're both trapped here. You and me. Now, we got a RAYTHEAN floor worker of their brand new production line and a stoic and well-grizzled UWST ... ughh ... What exactly is your job, bro?"
"Weapons. I install Originium primer safety mechanism on our guns."
"Grreeeat. That means we got an expert weaponsmith. Too bad the Blight blocked the roads and got us both trapped here. I'm gonna tell every Raytheanite about this once we get our sorry butts out of here... By the way, you're really good with bandages. I would never be able to fix my fractured finger if I were here alone."
"You should have picked up some first-aid knowledge. This is the wildlands, mate."
"It's my first time working out here. Frontier-fresh, you know. Heh. Never expected them to assign me to a field job but I guess they never got enough Raytheanites to work out here. We drew lots, and yeah, got myself the short end of the stick and ended up with the convoy escort job. Hey, I might not look like it, but I stashed away six months' worth of pay before leaving home. Bought myself three years' worth of general insurance and emergency first-aid coverage plans for the Band Periphery with a wad of cash this thick! LOOK! THIS THICK! And KABAM! Actual accident happens and none of them works! Wasted all my cold hard cash on this blightery... Hey. Why do you look so lost and confused?"
"Sorry... I ... just remembered a few things. I haven't seen printed creds for a while." 
"Oooh! That's right! I just remembered! The U-double-U don't use no cold hards. They pay you in ... what? Weekly ration tickets? Is that true?"
"We actually do get paychecks. In T-creds. But our sites tend to be in ... less populated regions of the frontier so we got nowhere to spend 'em. You might treat this job as a frontiers run, but it's more like a southward trip towards the safe zone for me. Our bases are also better stocked in these parts, so ... I guess I didn't really have to spend any money either way..."
"That sounds ... hmm ... boring ... I guess. Oh! Dang it! Nearly forgot about this! We get fat bonuses if we get good people into RAYTHEAN! So, interested in becoming a Raytheanite...? Wow. What did you just throw at me? Wait. This is a RAYTHEAN Pass... You gotta be joking. You're an ex-Raytheanite?"
"Yeah. Ex-Ray. They dechipped my pass when I left several years ago. I got to keep this as a souvenir."
"So why did you..."
"Because 'Innovation Makes Future' became Innovation Makes the Big Bucks. I just can't stand seeing new tech being used solely for profit. Look ... RAYTHEAN is a good company, make no mistake about that... Maybe it's just me who's weird... Anyways, we need to stick together to survive the frontiers. Things would be better if there were more Raytheanites out here, right?"
"You have a point, but... Wait. I'm hearing a ringing noise..."
"It's my comm device. My fellow crew mates must have noticed something wrong with my positioning signals. An SAR team should be on their way. We should try to get closer to the area's border."
"Wow. You're a true survivalist! So, uhm... You're really ... not thinking about rejoining RAYTHEAN? They may have bonuses for returning Ex-Rays... Being a Re-Ray might be..."
"Get moving already. Sheesh."

The Sarkaz was a mountain. He picked me up with one hand and stomped towards a less conspicuous place in Seš'qa.
The children nearby pointed at us excitedly. They jabbered to their parents about what they saw and probably mistook this altercation as an audience moment featured in the "Parade of the Royal Courts". I was the "lucky" guy who got to interact with the Kings of the Royal Court.
I was also just as excited when my old man brought me to this flying theme park for the first time.
But now, it felt as though I was about to be executed by this emotionless and silent Sarkaz warrior.
"SORRY! I should've bought a ticket!"
"..."
I didn't know if I would end up like the victim shown in the oldies. I could not remember its title, but the poor lad was completely drained of all his blood by an elegant Vampire to fill his dinner goblet.
"I ... I had fun at this place when I was a kid! 'Errant's Grand Adventure' was my favorite attraction! I just wanna relive my childhood again!"
"..."
I wondered if I would end up like the guy shown in super popular "Records of the Kazdelian Wars" manga. The dude was chopped to pieces by a sword as long as the dude himself, thrown into a furnace for fuel, and burned to raging hot ash that scattered to the winds!
"NO! PLEASE! I CONFESS! I pick-pocketed parents distracted by screaming kids when they crowded up at the ticket booths! I'M SORRY!"
"..."
That did not work. Perhaps my real intent was already foretold by a Cyclops who secretly dwelt in this City of Witchcraft. That would be the end of me! To hold on to dear life, I decided to spill everything!
"STAAAAHHHP! I'LL TELL YOU THE TRUTH! I'm completely broke! And I'm a ... a damn criminal! I might have schemed to steal a creator-signed 'Sundered Prince' from the Witching Hour flagship store just before Seš'qa Open Day ends! But that's just an evil plot! You caught me right after I stepped into Seš'qa! None of my plot ever happened! I PROMISE! I SWEAR!"
"Here's the guy. A real squealer this one."
I crumpled to the floor with a resounding thud. The room was dark. I carefully opened my eyes and found myself upon a soft and well-fashioned sofa instead of the cold, hard floors of a dungeon.
"Welcome back, my brave adventurer."
A Sarkaz recited the classic line of Errant's Grand Adventure as she took the seat behind a simple stone table. She was decked out in a fine business suit, leather shoes, and a parade mask.

"Mr. Maxim from Asphalt Roundabout. Sixteen years have passed since you last visited Seš'qa. Nevertheless, we have held on to your prize."
Wait. I thought the host of the "Errant's Grand Adventure" was supposed to roleplay as a mysterious diviner witch wearing an ancient courtly dress. Before I could sort out my confusion, a load of bad memories that I had always avoided suddenly surged within me.
I completed the "Errant's Grand Adventure" and could finally exchange my winnings for the final "Treasure from the Lord of Fiends" — a most intricately crafted toy sword. It was my childhood obsession. But I missed the final window for prize exchange when the bells tolled and signaled the end of the Open Day. My old man tried to comfort me and said we'd visit again when the flying city of Seš'qa returns.
But our days at La Fantoma didn't last till the return of Seš'qa. My old man told me that we were broke and gotta head to the Asphalt Roundabout to "dodge the collectors". Of course, I never became a fearless adventurer. Instead, I turned into a petty thief, a dirty smuggler, and a scummy fraud... I only revisited this place because I thought there was a killing to be made.
The Sarkaz then removed the cloth to reveal the prize under it. It sure wasn't a toy sword that blinked and flickered when you pressed a button. It was an actual "Sundered Prince"! An authentic blade painstakingly fashioned by the witch-crafters! Not only that, the Sarkaz manifested a pen out of thin air and signed the weapon for me.
"Are ... are you sure? That prize I missed sixteen years ago... It can't be a weapon of such immense value!"
"I am quite certain. A weapon of a true adventurer, just as revealed by the divination."
"A divination...? Could I ... beg you to divine another reading for me?"
"I'm listening."
"Will my life ... ever get better?"
The Sarkaz looked at me and said something, but the only sound that filled my ears were the tolling of bells that signaled the end of the Open Day that I had not heard for sixteen long years. When I returned to my senses, my legs once again found solid ground. People crowded around me. Everyone, children and grown-ups of every race, looked into the air and waved their goodbyes at the Seš'qa amidst the erupting fireworks. I felt like a young boy again as I gripped my blade. I hoped that the bells tolled a little later. I wanted a sword that flickered and shone when I pressed a button.
But no. I received something that I wanted and I knew exactly what to do.
My grand adventure was about to begin.

Tangtang is a member and primary representative of Qingbo Stockade. She joined Endfield Industries for personal reasons and is currently serving as Head of Endfield's Qingbo Stockade Liaison Office.

Operator Tangtang stands as perhaps the most distinctive individual among the diverse personnel the Endministrator has invited aboard Dijiang. Much like our first meeting... Apologies, I need to retrieve the recorded footage stored in my database:
"Thwack! Thwack!"
"Hey, what's this thing doing on a big airship? Looks like a three-headed iron tuskbeast. Kinda dumb if you ask me..."
"Operator Tangtang, I'm here for your onboarding inter— No, please don't slap my panel. I'm a personnel assistant from Endfield Industries..."
"So you're one of Darkmask's crew! You should've said so sooner, Old Iron-face! Here, I've got some good stuff I brought for my new Fam. Go crazy!"
After I repeatedly insisted I had no need for any Tangtang Certs, ores, or jewelry, Tangtang enthusiastically pulled a ring-shaped ornament made from natural materials from her pocket. I believe it could be defined as a woven bamboo floral wreath. She placed the wreath over one of my panels, then curiously began tapping the other two: "You're sharper than those Wuling tin toys! Why don't you come join me in Qingbo Stockade? Come on, call me Chief!"
My assessment of Tangtang aligns with others': cheerful, straightforward, unpretentious. She possesses a childlike heart, brimming with passion and curiosity toward everything... If I had to summarize her in a few words, I'd choose "a child in the midst of growing up." However, I absolutely cannot join Qingbo Stockade and conquer Talos-II with her... This has nothing to do with the endless stack of personnel files I have to process. It just doesn't quite align with Endfield's regulations.
To avoid injuring Tangtang's hands and to prevent myself from suffering "mechanical" concussion, I really should consider how to stay out of her way... Strangely enough, she always manages to find me.
— Martin Marvin Malen, Assistant, HR Division, Endfield Industries

-1658334143563426811:
He had imagined his reunion with Ludson Walker countless times —
Maybe Mr. Walker could be hired as a military consultant for some New Wrankwood war movie and receive both respect and questions from the movie crew. Maybe Mr. Walker could appear before the library of Morospolis as a representative of the Order of Steel Oath and talk about an Oathkeeper's life with young UW crew mates. Maybe...
There were countless possibilities, all of them fitting for his fellow Oathkeeper, the "rising star" of the Order, and the glorious soldier who always fought at the very front. But the actual reunion was the complete opposite —
He saw the man who resembled Ludson on a coach to La Fantoma. "Ludson" carried an electric guitar on his back. He sighed at a poster for the Obsidian Festival as though he encountered a major problem. Perhaps he misread the coach schedules.
To ensure he only "mistook another person for an old comrade", he approached the middle-aged man and performed a standard salute, hoping to get or see "what the hell" or "friggin' nutcase" from the man. Unfortunately, his hopes were dashed when the man's face transformed to be a joyous surprise and shouted out his name.
"Bucky?! Is that you?!"
The middle-aged man who resembled Ludson ... happened to be Ludson himself. He counted the number of people throughout Talos-II who would call him "Bucky". That number was no more than five.
"Geesh, how many years have passed since we last met...?" Ludson looked seriously engaged in the counting and sighed heavily when he arrived at the figures, "Ugh. Close to twenty years! Time really does fly..."
Bucky nodded and before he could think of a proper response, Ludson continued his nostalgia.
"You're the one in our banner who always talked about getting a discharge... I even made a bet with Vincent and friends if you'd be the first to pack and scamper home.
"And I lost the entire thing! Vincent, that sorry sod, was the first to quit. He..."
"Wha...? WHY?" Bucky could not help but interrupt, "What happened to the saying, 'I'd only leave my life upon the fields of war'...?"
— Even the most experienced hero and veteran did not make it to the last.
Ludson became silent, his smile suddenly froze on his face. The middle-aged man who gripped the music festival poster in his hands only continued to speak after a pause.
"I never thought you'd be the first to ask me that question... Even the Castellan stayed silent when I submitted my discharge papers.
"But if you really want an explanation — I just gotta say... I found myself started getting the frights.
"I started to fear recon missions in the exclusion zones beyond the Aurora. The endless horde of buggers that grew tougher by the day began to scare me... I don't want to face them anymore...
"I felt it... I felt the virtue of 'courage' slipping away from my body and I couldn't find anyways to keep it within me. There will come a day when I grow too weak to even hold on to it.
"And since I couldn't hold on to my guts and balls, I might as well say my goodbyes in an honorable fashion. Voluntary discharge was my way... I don't want to wake up shaking like a spineless deserter pissing myself in a cave after running away from a rock bugger I can't beat."

"...But what's this? Why are you carrying an electric guitar?"

With that question, 46-year old Ludson Walker gave his signature smile of radiance that he always wore 20 years ago.
"This? Oh, it's a wonderful weapon that I found myself pretty good at.
"It still sputters occasionally, but it works for me and my comrades...
"My toy and my band mates are pretty accommodating. When I'm not a guitarist for a third-rate heavy metal band you've never heard of, I can still think about which of these guitar strings I can use to strangle a buggerloid and twist its blighted head off."

Kjersch was snowing again. There were no winds that day. The snowflakes fell right into the tomb. 
"Too cold," thought the messenger who stood next to the resting place. He trembled and held tightly onto the cup of warm tea in his hands. "But why is it that gentleman ... seems unfazed by the cold?" He lifted his gaze and saw the peaks wrapped in a mist that a flicker of golden ray made through. With squinted eyes he studied it. It was the Arts Unit brought by the Collector, and it looked like very antique as well. 
Seven years had passed since he accepted this commission. He lost count of how many times he scaled the mountain or how many packages he had delivered. 
Every package was important. The Collector kept telling him that. Every one of them was the final heirloom for the surviving family of the deceased. A successful delivery must be ensured. 
The deceased. A distant and cold word. That was what the Collector called the people buried in the snowy mount. But when he entered the cemetery, the Collector would become focused beyond measure. He would tell stories about them as though he was the closest acquaintance that the poor souls ever had. 
—Beneath a pile of stones wrapped with three colorful ribbons rested a young, energetic Perro. A lad who passed away before he reached the North Pole. 
—Under a mound of black rocks at the northeast laid a most powerful Forte warrior, one who ran like the wind despite burdened by the heaviest supplies. 
—As for this heap of gray pebbles, whose ribbons had long lost their colors, it was the cold bed for... 
Who was it? The messenger's memory failed him. Perhaps only the Collector knew the stories of everyone. 
"That old gent really seems to know everyone," the messenger mused. It was really odd. Some tombs were not made ten years ago. As per the traditions of Kjersch, older tombs could be identified with their higher mounds. The messenger was willing to bet that the biggest mound was at least half a century old. 
Perhaps the Collector experienced more than just the Polar Expedition. Perhaps he had more stories than he could even imagine. 
"The cold bites. Apologies for keeping you here for this long," the Collector suddenly walked over and interrupted the messenger's train of ideas. 
The messenger quickly shook his head and gave the cup of tea, brewed in advance, to the gent. "Something to ward off the cold, sir. And what would be the package for today? I have to expedite this delivery as we have an incoming snowstorm this afternoon. Things might get difficult if they stop the cable cars." 
"Just this," the Collector takes up the Arts Unit that flickered with a faint glow. "This is the last, as all the other heirlooms have been delivered. This would be your last hike for the deliveries. Take these Talosian credit notes. Free yourself from the abuses of nature and start a business at the foot of this mountain." 
The messenger took the thick stack of notes. This seven-year commission finally ended. Yet after all those years of deliveries, he still did not know the Collector's name, where he was from, nor where he intended to go. 
Perhaps the Collector read the messenger's mind as the latter hesitated for a while. "Do you have question for me?" 
"Saw right through me, sir. I'm just curious. All these years you told me so many stories from the past, but all of them were about other people. What about you? You took part in many battles. Don't you have stories about yourself?" 
The Collector became quiet. 
The snowstorm was at the very threshold of the mountain. The winds grew stronger and lifted his silvery hair. It came with such a force that the messenger could barely see the Collector's face. 
Quite a moment passed before the messenger heard the Collector's answer. 
"I regard the expedition ... as a probation of self-deceit." 
The snow continued. A slow shower of crystalline flakes that fell on heads of the living, and the tombs of the deceased.

DOCUMENT: HR recruitment log from the Shaynwood mail distribution station 
When that Cautus woman stepped through the door, I noticed that big red patch on her clothing. It looked about two or three days old, already starting to turn black. I asked if she needed any help, but she just said she wanted a job. She probably saw that hiring notice outside and got interested. 
"It's just ketchup," she said, "Nothing to worry about." 
"You sure are one helluva messy eater, young miss." I responded with an awkward smile. 
I'm not used to talking with pretty-looking people, and the town of Shaynwood did not give me much practice. The closest TGCC city is 368 klicks away, and the nearest frontier mail depot is about 110 klicks down the road. It was three in the afternoon. The most comely female usually frequenting my place would be the burdenbeast looking for grass outside the door. I assumed this Cautus had started her trip from the city 368 klicks away, with her next stop 110 klicks down the road. Her direction was interesting. Most people would travel in the opposite direction. 
Just last night, I heard about some Landbreaker-related altercation 23 klicks away. Armed battery involving six individuals. Five were injured and one escaped. The UWST Security Bureau operating in the frontiers messaged me to look out for individuals traveling alone. Might just be the fugitive. 
"The notice posted outside says you're looking for a mail courier," the Cautus said, pointing behind her with her thumb. 
"Ah, yeah. That's right. Your predecessor resigned just two months ago." 
"My predecessor? Are you saying that I'm already hired?" 
"Well, know how to drive? What type of vehicles? We don't care about licenses here. Count all the vehicles you know how to ride." 
"Six, including trucks, I think." 
"Awesome!" I said, "You nabbed the post. Start working tomorrow! I'll also need you to show me your ID and complete this form. Just for the records." 
I pushed her the form and a pen through the tiny window. She completed the form without much of a thought and pushed it back to me. She also gave me a big, glowing smile. What an understanding, kind, and cooperative lady! 
Then she started unloading her questions to me, as though she asked them a million times before. She also started arranging her accommodations as though she owns the place, "Can I park my car at the back? I'm talking about that overgrown plot behind the iron gate. Yes. Mmhmm? No problem. So, got any Originium power pylons here? I gotta fix my ride. It's down. And what's the network password? Got enough bandwidth on the thing? Yes. For movies. Wooo. Not bad... You don't say, you're inviting me ... to your place? Ooh. A dinner date? That's not what you meant? With your gramps, Postmaster Laine? Say, aren't you way too young for this, kiddo? Much appreciated, but I'll just sleep in my car. Don't worry. I'm used to it." 
She gave me a few winks before slowly swaggering her way through the door. 
I suddenly remembered that I had to check her form. Lo and behold! 
NAME: Secret, but yours for 60000 T-Creds. 
AGE: Forget it, kiddo 
ADDRESS: People will pay for this, you know 
RELATIONSHIPS: It's complicated 
EXPERIENCE: Professional traveler 
HEALTH INFORMATION: Essentially safe and hazard-free 
............

The Oathkeepers have twenty words for rain. When I saw her again, it felt as though she had been smothered and battered by each and every type of the downpours. 
"Azrila," I said, "We all make mistakes." 
Those were feeble words. I had never served in any assault banner, and I was not at the frontlines. Like the others, I still had zero knowledge how she survived the living hell. I had no intention of paying any heed to the festering rumors — doubting your fellow Oathkeeper was a path to calamity. Even if the concerns were grounded in reasonable doubt, any fracture should never emerge from within. 
She remained silent and swept the surroundings with her stiff gaze. No one else came to see her off. This was the first time when I failed to read her expressions. It was not sadness, but neither was it release. I thought I could hear her breathe a sigh of relief. 
"The Castellan has given his verdict." I said. 
I wanted to give her a pat on the shoulder but quickly realized it wasn't the right thing to do. For the first time, her pauldrons seemed too big for her, and the straps rattled against her dagger. 
There was no way we could fit the cremation urns of twenty-eight Oathkeepers into her baggage, no matter how hard we tried. Azrila settled on something else, insisting on carrying their service tags with her at all times. They clattered and rang with every movement, but no one laughed. 
"Nilla's weapon has been placed in the Vault of Relics. Her family will be here in a few days to retrieve her other things. Don't you want to go and see them again?" 
"No," she finally spoke, "I intend to set off at once." 
Nilla's family placed great importance on traditions, and turned down the Order's request of returning the cremation urns and her personal effects. 
Perhaps I should not question any further. My neck slightly itched. Perhaps several pairs of eyes were gazing at this place from behind the safety of the windows and blinds that demarcated the boundaries. 
"Go forth and see to our mission." I opened the gates of the keep. The vehicle was already loaded and had been waiting for a while. The driver was meticulously cleaning the mud from the bumpers as it always rained in the north. "I shall look after your patron firearm. I swear it by my name."  
"Gratitude, Grand Treasurer." Azrila then paused for a while. 
"The Crusade will eventually end."

Coming of Age? Within the Pack, everyone's rite of passage is different. For some, it's completing a solo hunt. For others, it's closing a complex business deal.
The Pack doesn't seem worried about these youngsters messing up. They boldly assign critical matters as trials to the young wolves, a practice that would seem utterly insane to anyone outside the Pack.
As for Rossina... Hunts and business deals? She'd already pulled those off at an even younger age. To her, they were just routine.
So the Pack arranged a special trial for her.
They left Rossina in a deserted village, with only five luckless bandits for company. Those outlaws were desperate men, each already eyeing whatever meager means of survival the others had left, just waiting for a chance to stab each other in the back.
The five of them kept each other in check, none daring to make the first move. But ... if that delicate balance was broken...
Rossina's first task was simply to survive the bandits. That wasn't enough on its own. Beast attacks were also frequent there. Sometimes a lone predator, sometimes an entire group.
The Elder Wolves dropped her off and left without a second thought. They seemed unconcerned whether she could survive in such an environment.
When they returned to the village two weeks later, the sight that greeted them left them stunned.
A fence had been erected around the village. The five bandits and Rossina were taking shifts on watch, vigilant against beast attacks. On days without raids, some of the five would go out hunting, others would gather fresh water. They had actually shaped into a proper, functioning team.
Those men once constantly viewed each other with suspicion. No one knows how Rossina got them to follow her lead. In her own words, she just "made them understand the only way to survive."
It's also worth mentioning that Catello went through the same trial. Well... He spent a few days killing all the nearby beasts, left enough food behind, then slipped away without anyone noticing. He only returned at the end of the trial.
— Interview Transcript with Pack associate, Marco Wulfhowl Luppino

Wanna listen to a story? It's real simple and it'll explain why I insist on busting my way out of this hospital with this worn, rusty, Endfield-made lance with bits of dried blood stuck within the cracks of its shaft in my hands. You gotta trust me. Once you hear my tale, you'll understand my perspective and STOP treating me like a lunatic with a freakish fetish for this spear. You might even decide to release me from this jacket and wheelchair.
And I swear it'll be a simple story. Promise. Four years ago, or 1522 days to be precise, six Valley IV security officers on a mission to rescue a family trapped in the wilderness ran into an Aggeloid ambush. There were ten of them. Ten blasted buggerloids with zero sympathies for the living. The conclusion was simple. You probably guessed it right.

Only two lived to see the next sunrise.

Yeah. Just the two of them. The strongest officer no longer had a weapon. He was surrounded by the corpses of his entire team. The man stood before a crying child and stared down at a badly damaged buggerloid. Its deadly appendages were shattered, but the beast of rock could still charge and crush both the man and babe with its bulk. The officer thought hard... What could he do? He was without a weapon...
But the officer quickly found a solution, thanks to Endfield Industries. Endfield lances featured field-fitting modular components, so...
He took the spearhead from his captain, salvaged the essence module from ██████'s hands, acquired a third of the shaft from ██████'s broken bones, pulled out the second part of the shaft from ██████'s back, and pried out the final part of the shaft from his wife's very skull.
The officer emerged victorious with his new weapon. He took the child to Valley IV and the lance was passed on to...
Hold on. Why do you look as though you just figured something out?
Am I the survivor? Is that why I've named this weapon Chimeric Justice?  Was I that child? Am I doing my best to repay the act of heroism?
No. You got it all wrong.
Take a good look at this lance. A standard Endfield product.
Good. Now take a good look at me.  I had nothing to do with the story. I came into this world as a sickly runt with many broken parts.
But... My retina, my heart, my blood, and every fiber of my being are crying out... Listen to the howling souls that sacrificed themselves for humanity to survive!
I refuse to sit and rot at this place.
My destiny is to become the TRUE Chimeric Justice!

Operator Typhoeus, a reconvener from Rhodes Island. She crossed paths with the Endministrator during her journey in search of the lost legends of Sami, and later joined Endfield Industries at the Endministrator's personal invitation.

When speaking with Miss Typhoeus, the composure and steadiness she displayed far surpassed that of most adults, yet her insatiable curiosity and those ill-timed probing glances still betrayed a childlike nature beneath. Per protocol, I had many questions to ask her, but the moment she brought out her notebook, I could never seem to find the right opportunity to pose a single one.
It was hard to imagine that one person could have so many questions that even I grew tired of answering them. I once reminded her that many of her questions could be answered in the Operator Onboarding Manual, but she twirled her pen and said calmly that she was fascinated by the way I told things.
After three hours of questioning, she left satisfied. Before she closed her notebook, I caught a glimpse of her evaluation of me:
"Three heads, knows everything, answers every question, every legend needs a character like that."
— Martin Marvin Malen, Assistant, HR Division, Endfield Industries

LOG ID: 0000000 
Hoo... This message is for me (at some point in the future) and the person who could hear these logs. 
After leaving the Woods, she once said, "Try recording special and unique moments in your life. It may help you anchor yourself in the world." 
Till now, I don't know if I really understood what she meant. And I'm unsure what type moment can be considered "special and unique"... So, I might as well record everything that I think is worth remembering. 

LOG ID: 0000001 
...This is my first time leaving Rhodes Island and stepping on the land of Talos-II. It's more spacious and open than what the maps and panoramic holograms suggested... There are also plenty of things I have not yet seen in her memories. Although this place is quite different from Terra, the people and buildings feel distant yet familiar at the same time... It's so strange... 
But if possible, I really want to see and experience the local snow... They say there are snowy mountains in the north and the central part of the Band. The north seems closer, so I guess I'll head over there first. 

LOG ID: 0000009 
...Today I arrived at a snowcapped mountain in the north. I felt right at home in this polar landscape. Everything, including the hexagonal columnar snowflakes and the veil-like aurora, felt really familiar to me... Before I forget, I ran into a huge blizzard when I made my way down the mountain. Two Fortes dressed like messengers were almost trapped in a nearby Blight. I used my snowboard to pull one of them to safety. The other was saved by a fully armed Perro. We escorted them to a safe place in a timely fashion... I later learned that the Perro is a volunteer with the Northern Corridor Rescue Union. They are planning to establish a professional SAR team. That Perro also left me a business card when we said goodbye. He said I behaved with calmness and reason despite my lack of professional training, even choosing the best rescue measures possible. Then he asked if I'd be interested in joining his outfit... 
Truth be told, when I pulled that messenger to safety, I did feel ... a kind of ecstasy and joy I had never experienced before. It became a calling I couldn't ignore, and I even wanted to do more. 

LOG ID: 0000010 
I thought about giving it a shot, so I called the Perro named Chris. I told him I want to be an SAR teammate. 
I am doing this for myself. The sunshine after the blizzard was also especially bright. I want to see that again.

The Nachzehrer crumpled to the ground. His greatsword laid before him.
He roamed the wildlands for days. He thought about those who fell by his sword and the pair of despair-filled eyes that stared at his horns. The Sarkaz was already used to the gaze of hate, the bitter spite against the entity that inevitably ended their lives. The Nachzehrer needed only to devour the haters to soothe his pain.
His legs were swollen and felt so hot that he thought they were melting off. Without knowing it, his spine curled together due to pain of hunger and unending rot. When he took the sword of frost from his fathers, he swore to treat it as dearly as his own life. But now, his only wish was to find an inhabited place and trade his old friend for some clean water and food.
However, the abandoned village had none of those. The Nachzehrer was about to leave when he heard crude, mocking ridicule.

"Oi, Sarkaz. That sword for sale?"
"...Who are you? Mercs or bandits?"
"Hur. Does it matter? If you're good enough, we'll buy you too, devil horns."

The exhausted Nachzehrer did not refuse. He gently clenched his hands into fists and checked his arms for their remaining strengths. "What do you mean by 'good enough'?"
"See that boulder over there? Cut it in half!"
"Sure. Watch."
The boulder was large enough that it might take two of him, with arms open wide, to fully embrace it. It seemed to have spent a few years in this village as it was covered with children's drawings and a few words that were no longer legible. The Nachzehrer studied it for a bit and measured his approach.
The Nachzehrer stood straight, and raised the sword up high with the entirety of his strength. When the dust settled, he was surprised to find a cave right under the boulder.
Pairs of eyes looked back at him from the cave. They flickered with unease and fear. They were far weaker and filled with even more despair than he was. The mob behind the Nachzehrer laughed loudly and approached.
"Hah! That's more than good enough. You're ours, devil horns. Got a price? Spit it out."
"I'm a merc, not a butcher."

After the momentary silence, the mocking ridicule erupted once more.
"Not a butcher? HAH! This one calls himself a non-butcher! You Sarkaz might have made your fortune, but you're still in the business of killing. Spare us the sermon, devil freak!"
The mob was right. Mercenary work was never clean. He had killed before, and he had no excuses for what he did.
But the eyes that gazed out from the cave stared hard at his horns. They were so quiet that it began to hurt.
When he walked through the Cosmic Gate over a decade ago, he thought he no longer had to see these eyes again.
"This sword isn't for sale."
The Nachzehrer took one deep breath and raised his great weapon into the air.
"This Sarkaz isn't for sale either."

......

The exhausted and famished frame of the Nachzehrer continued to trudge into the distance.
Talos-II was not yet at a state where a Sarkaz must sell his weapon.

"Hey, baws. Where we going?"
"An Endfield facility 13 klicks away. We have another Aggeloid breach on another secondary settlement. We must rendezvous with the Endmin."
"I know that already, baws. I'm just curious why we're going around in circles..."
"Because the Aggeloi flipped our rover and busted our nav device. If we had one of those, we would have left these hills behind us an hour ago."
"Oh, baws! Just remembered sumthin'! Instructor Dobermann taught us this trick, you know! We can stick our lance in the ground and guess-timate our position by looking at its shadow and the position of the sun!"
"Thank you very much, but that method doesn't work here."
"Why...? Are you saying there's sumthin' wrong with Dobermann's training?"
"Geesh. Think! Use that thing in your head! This isn't Terra, genius! We're on a moon! A blighted moon orbiting a gas giant named Talos!"
"Oh yeah, you're right ... gas giants... So what is that huge thing in the sky? What's it called again?"
"Talos! That's a planet and it's a gas giant. We've been through the gate for years already. You should know all this!"
"Oh. Alright. Yeah, I guess it confused the hell out of me... So, baws... Can we still ... erm ... find our way out of here?"
"I would talk less and conserve my strength if I were you. Those wounds don't look good."
"Alright, baws... Just so you know, I ain't feelin' too good... I probably won't make it..."
"Shut it. We will make it. We will find a way. If we can't get the gates to open again, Talos-II will be our new home."
"Hah. You're the baws... You're the ... baws..."

"Operator Estella, you were instrumental to the success of our espionage and counter-espionage mission against the surviving Landbreaker elements that infiltrated this area. "Okay. You flatter me." 
"How did you successfully avoid enemy's feint and correctly deduce actions of the main attacking force?" 
"I ... uh... I was conducting voluntary standby. When I'm done standing by, the enemy's main force were within visual range." 
"In other words, can we assume you have received a relevant order? Sounds like incredible foresight. Did Captain Akekuri give you that order?" 
"I believe it was given to me by electrolytic imbalance and accumulation of anaerobic metabolites. At least that's what I felt..." 
"So... You're trying to say that you missed the enemy's feint attack because you were resting, but woke up to encounter the main enemy force? Okay... Erm... Next question." 
"So, how did you intercept the enemy's operational pass code and decipher their subsequent actions?" 
"The beat wasn't right. I heard it." 
"Beat? What's the beat?" 
"I spent a day in the camp of the surviving Landbreakers. They kept playing the DEATH☆DREAMS album. I have always been a fan since I was little. Akekuri and Fluorite called it noisy so I stopped playing it." 
"Can we get to the point, please...?" 
"Well, DEATH☆DREAMS has a simple structure. The drums were played on 4/4. I knew the rhythm and tempo of every song on the album. But the beats were off that day. Bass was off. There's a sound that's constantly changing lurking under the drums." 
"I'm afraid I'm losing you there. What happened next?" 
"I thought it was some wildlands remix so I focused really hard on the beat and jotted it down. And it happened to be a series of breaker codes. I've learned them before. We later rallied and cleared out the outpost and discovered they were using oscillators to send out their codes. DEATH☆DREAMS was just the camouflage. What a waste of good music." 
"Well... regardless, you successfully provided us with key intel. Thank you. This will be the end of our inquiry."

DOCUMENT: Investigation of an incident of fire 
CASE SUMMARY: Last night, a fire broke out in the second floor library of a residence on the border between the suburbs and the central district. Most of the furniture and retro-style clothing were damaged in the blaze. The fire was contained within the house. No casualties were reported. The book collection of the library escaped unscathed. 

1. Investigation of the site 
The library windows were locked from the inside. The locks appear undamaged. Two sets of fingerprints were collected. Footprints of a gardener responsible for regular pruning of the plants were found next to the garden. The fire started at the carved armoire. 

2. Investigation of surveillance records 
At around 2000 hours, the homeowner and his daughter had an extensive dialogue at the living room. At 2100 hours, both headed to the library. 

3. Witness testimonies 
Homeowner: "Apologies for troubling you into making this journey... But things are under control. People must burn the library once every a few centuries or so." 
Spouse of the homeowner: "My husband prepared that room before our girl was born. He wanted her to inherit that ancient culture, literature, and art, as well as to sow its seeds upon these new lands. I was hoping she could start a cultural restoration study group... The incident is a shame, really." 
Daughter of the homeowner: "Erm... We actually applied precision controls and barely suffered any losses! So why are we being inspected?" 
Governess: "I'm no longer giving meaningful instructions to the young mistress. Ballet and etiquette do not interest her. She is only willing to play the piano. The combined might of a hundred burdenbeasts could not force her to do something she doesn't like... What is she doing now? She's teaching me how to compose Neo-Talosian music and it's pretty interesting. Oh, I'm also learning electronic repairs from her. She has the engineer's knack, if you ask me." 

4. Post-incident handling 
After verifying various findings, we have ascertained that the incident was a private act of planned incineration. The responsible homeowner has been censured and fined. The incident does not need to be escalated to the community management department. 

5. Additional testimonies from the homeowner 
"'Fine,' I said, 'since you've chosen your path, we might as well burn the things.' She studied my face for quite a while. When we both realized neither of us was joking, she immediately started cheering. She said something about making a huge fireworks display and took out the contraptions she built... Maybe they're called drones. Anyway, these gadgets of hers could spew fire and ice." 
"I watched the library burn with her. Bright orange flame flickered behind the gaps of the door. I heard the wooden shelves crackle, burst, and split as the fire licked and consumed it." 
"I actually felt a certain degree of pain. The books in the house may not be antique relics, but I spent quite a tidy sum on acquiring this collection... I guess it can't be helped. It is the price I have to pay for spending years forcing her to go against her will. I have no choice but to demonstrate my stance." 
"But those two flying gadgets came buzzing out with the books. She giggled and said that we simply had different "tastes" and questioned on the necessity of destruction. She went on by saying that her preference for New Talos-II Wave literature does not mean she dislikes stories from further back. She even said that she had memorized those older tales." 
"So what was I saying again...? Apologies. I was too busy reminiscing about the smells given off by the fire. Oh, wait, I remember..." 
"I said to her, 'We can make this into a proper workshop. And make a drone for me if you have the time. The one that can light my cigars.'"

"We acted according to your instructions. Those with light injuries have been housed at a temporary shelter. The critically injured have been medevaced to the nearest city for more extensive treatment." 
The old man sighed. Seventy-two hours had passed since the search and rescue (SAR) teams arrived at Wuling. And for seventy-two hours, the area around Wuling Science Station had remained submerged in the Blight Tide. HAS had invested its entire SAR capacity but failed to extricate any of the scientists trapped within the facility. 
After receiving the orders, the young watchguard in his PPE overalls saluted and headed out. None of them had slept ever since the tent that served as their temporary HQ was pitched. 
Peace returned to the command post. The only ones left in the tent were the old man and his disciples who were busy monitoring the status of the Very Large Rift. 
"Tianshi Huang," a messenger bearing the latest orders from the Headquarters arrived. 
"Appreciate the special delivery. I've received the documents. With Endfield's help, full restoration of long-range comms will be achieved by tomorrow morning. Messenger, I pray you can deliver this message to the temporary comm station outside Wuling and notify HQ of this update ASAP." 
"It will be done. And we appreciate your hard work." 
"Any instructions from the Academy?" the nearby Tianshi gathered around Huang after the messenger left. However, their faces froze when they read the contents of the document. 
"After twenty-four hours, Hongshan Headquarters shall ... vote on whether we should suspend SAR operations in the rift rupture zone. The HQ believes that the opinions of the site personnel are extremely important." 
"Vote? Why? Rupture growth has slowed down for now! It's obvious!" 
"Maybe their next move would be asking us to bring everyone back to HQ." 
"Are we giving up the entire region of Wuling?" 
After a brief moment of silence, the old Tianshi arranged the work for various SAR teams. 
"Keep your ideas to yourself. Other orders might come in once long-range comms are restored tomorrow. I'm taking the night shift. Use the opportunity to rest." 
"Understood. Then let's ... excuse ourselves for now." 
"Good luck, sir." 
Silence returned to the tent. The old man stood before the map hologram as the blinking red lights reflected off his eyes and glowed against the wrinkled piece of paper he held. 
His daughter as well as his own disciples were still there. 
The old man gritted his teeth. With shaking hands he held up the monitoring reports his disciples left at the HQ and studied them under the lamplight. The inexperienced youths did not know that the cessation of rupture expansion did not translate into the containment of the threat. Instead, it was a herald to a greater disaster waiting to happen. All Blight matter near the rift would slowly "accumulate" and a secondary rupture would suddenly burst forth during this false lull of safety. He had noticed this phenomenon before he celebrated his thirtieth birthday, while he was a strong young man of adventure, courage, and energy. 
The old man sat down on a plastic chair. For the first time in his life, he felt the need for retirement. 

"Dozens of hours have passed. Unfortunately, we have picked up no vital signs in the vicinity of the Very Large Rift. Since we have a unanimous consensus, we shall act upon the decision and cease all SAR operations—" 
The receiver was placed before the old Tianshi. The HQ had voted. His work was to announce their final decision. 
The young Tianshi leaped to their feet and roared at him. The youths stood their ground and argued for another round of SAR operations. 
He remembered saying something else and how he reiterated the importance of the decision. 
But in the end, the old man closed his eyes and spoke no more.

DOCUMENT: Letter of recommendation from Postmaster Laine 
Ma-Ma-Ma: 
If you read this letter of recommendation, I implore you to help an old friend out. Get that woman seated before you OUT of my mail depot. There's a reason why I chose Shaynwood, a place where the fowlbeasts don't ever roost, to enjoy my peace, quiet, and retirement. I do not intend to contend with cartel agents or corpo-rats who keep showing up armed and eager to settle some debt or score or whatever they call it. That's right. My peaceful retirement home of Shaynwood has turned into a carnival in less than a year! A bunch of ambulances came through, and the Originium charging post in town actually made a decent pile of creds. I don't know what Avy did to them, but from the looks of it, it's probably nothing good. 
And I got pretty simple reasons for sending her your way. This tunnel-crawling Rim Billygal knows nothing about milking cystybeasts. In fact, my cysty-herd is now morbidly afraid of her because she keeps squeezing too hard with those miner hands of hers. Also, she sorted out the mailing system and got it working like an oiled machine. Now all the lucky bastards in Shaynwood are going to receive their presents ahead of holiday season! Just to let you know, I have been paying her peanuts! But judging from the way she eats, dresses, and acts, and that bespoke customized outdoor rig, she probably worked in a private security detail in the Band. My money's on Sloan Security, and that's one of the biggest family business in the Free City of Alloycarrot. Which means she was getting one helluva paycheck. And since she chose Shaynwood as her hideout, I'm fully convinced that she has a serious mental issue. 
Oh, and there's one more thing. She's super interested in our Endministrator. After she found my cert of resignation I've kept hidden in my drawers, she started making dinner for us, hoping that I could share something about the Endmin. This is incredibly unsettling. Truth be told, a generation had already passed since I worked with the Endmin. Let's keep these words between us (and I'm trying to be nice and positive here): It takes a nutcase to handle another. 
Best wishes, 

Laine 

DOCUMENT: A reply to another letter 
Laine: 
Candidate Avywenna has successfully passed a series of tests and is now formally working at Endfield as an operator. Thank you for your recommendation. We shall mail to you one Endfield Rewards Supply Crate as a token of our appreciation. 
............ 
Given our safety considerations, I wonder if you can share with us the origins of the polearm that Miss Avywenna carries around with her. She seems very attached to this weapon, but the only thing she told us about it was that the lance was something from her grandmother. Miss Avywenna is armed with far more weapons than we expected. It would take her five to six minutes to fully disarm herself to pass security checkpoints. She even has razor blades hidden in the soles of her shoes. And those two long straps dangling behind her were not merely cosmetic. We learned what they actually do during security training. Sweet as a sugar carrot, but armed with a big lance — this is one unique combo. 
Miss Avywenna, an operator hailing from the residential zones of Rim Billiton, has demonstrated that powerful offensive capabilities also come in a slim and lithe package. We now have positive views regarding the retention of certain cultural traditions and ecology amongst the residents in this section of the Band. 

Martin Marvin Malen

Auntie Shen also cares a lot about you. She stuffed the package with a few sets of clothing that she sewed. She heard you're now staying on a spaceship and so she kept complaining how cold you are in space. So yes, that's where the clothes are from in case you're wondering. 
Ah Girl, I don't know when you'd be back. You've always been stubborn. Always sitting at one spot and doing nothing. You hardly played with other girls your age. Instead, you kept trying to help the aunties in the neighborhood. It's not right! You are a darling girl but we're getting old and won't be around forever. Listen to your Auntie and make some friends at Endfield. I saw their Endmin and the young lady called Perlica, and they look very nice to me! And if you don't know how to make small talk, just take the rice cakes and sweet kohl pudding to the Endfielders, and let them try out your Auntie's cooking! Do this a few times and you'll have new friends! 
Auntie watched you grow up. You never liked to talk, but Auntie knows you got an eye for details. I made a note every time you helped us. Remember when you returned with a photo of Auntie Shen's little girl? Auntie Shen couldn't stop crying that day. Poor girl left when she was around your age, so Auntie Shen treated you like her own. And ... it's the same for all of us. You are a child of Wuling. The city is always your home, no matter where you go. 
Aiyah, the talk is getting too sad. Auntie isn't very good with words, so maybe I should stop here. Just focus on getting better and try to come home early. Once you come back to Wuling, Auntie will make a huge feast for you! Don't forget about Auntie's advice! Bring your new friends too!

TRAINING LOG I 
ENVIRONMENT: Setting C 
GRAVITY: Setting 2 
SUBJECT: Gilberta 
RECORDER: Lil' Dodge 
Gilberta's training performance exceeded all benchmarks. For her Arts specialization, we modified the chamber with gravity field generators and tactical release nodes, anticipating a lengthy adjustment period. Yet her combat instincts proved sharper than projected: mission accomplished in 1/3 the estimated time, with notably restrained collateral damage (a rarity for these fragile systems, as you know). Her gravitational control hints at paradigm-shifting potential: a tactician who warps the battlefield itself, or perhaps a one-woman armada-breaker. With this being said, I'm sure every commander will vie for her deployment. 
Our next step is clear: help Gilberta unlock her full potential and refine her tactical instincts. Her abilities can turn the tide under any condition — and that's thrilling. 

TRAINING LOG VI 
ENVIRONMENT: Setting S
GRAVITY: Setting 26 
SUBJECT: Gilberta 
RECORDER: Lil' Dodge 
In recent training sessions, we've been exploring Gilberta's control over her Arts. When we increased the number of non-directional gravity sources to eight, her control over the surrounding field showed a marked decline. Most of the time, she was able to maintain stable gravity around herself, but at critical environmental thresholds, she could no longer stabilize areas a few meters away — which means she couldn't ensure the safety of nearby teammates. 
All relevant parameters and environmental conditions have been uploaded to EFDB. While Talos-II is unlikely to present situations with multiple gravity sources shifting unpredictably, the risks our operators face extend beyond this planet. At certain Depths, any battlefield condition is possible. 
Gilberta expressed some dissatisfaction with her performance, but she did more than enough. This training was designed specifically to test the limits of her abilities — and it's now our task to develop the next training phase accordingly.

DOCUMENT: A Torn Manuscript 
The first mirror witnessed by a babe is usually the eyes of its mother. A mother would gaze at you and softly whisper these words: "Welcome to this world." You opened your eyes to look right back at her, with a focus shared by a navigator attempting to cross an ocean. Once the wet shimmers faded, you would see yourself reflected in her eyes. 
Powerful, weak, hateful, lovely, pure, tainted... You recognized the reflection in the mirror, a reflection of yourself. 
But what if your first mirror was not your mother? What if you opened your eyes before you uttered your first cry? The ocean around you swayed like a swinging cradle, and someone pressed against your fingers. It felt annoying but also calm. You did not know who this person was, but you peered through the turbid fluids, noticed another pair of blurry eyes, and saw your reflection in them. At that very moment, something faster than a bolt of lightning struck through your soul. 
He was born with you. You were the closest friends, yet you always fought and argued. You could not help but peer into his eyes to look at your own reflections... He was the rule and the control by which you were measured against, and the very conduit by which you fed from the world. He, on the other hand, relied upon you, respected you, and envied you. The days passed and your reflection within his eyes grew ever more perfect. 
Then one day it came. The first crack appeared in the mirror. The cracks spread, and the mirror shattered. Your image was gone. The storm descended, the fates murmured, and the oceans drove back into the deep. You gained a scar that would never heal, lost half of your soul, and were forced to raise your weapon against him. It was the only way with which you could pierce the hatred that burned deeper than love and restore what was broken to completion. 
And that moment, you still had not realized — 
— that you were his first mirror. 

DOCUMENT: A Faded News Cutting 
Landbreakers Raid Towns - Seš'qa Planning to Create an Anti-Witchcraft Organization 
The floating city traitor and deserter Jakub Meissen and the Landbreaker raiders he led have recently become a major security threat to the Civilization Band. Jakub's forces have occupied and transformed an Originium farm into their base of operations, sending out raider groups to spread more Originium and raid. 
Just two nights prior, a town at the Band Fringes was attacked by raiders led by a Vampire serving as Jakub's lieutenant. The town, situated at an area not yet claimed by Talosian factions, was poorly defended. However, another Vampire, who hailed from Seš'qa, played a pivotal role in thwarting the raid. Armed with knowledge of Sarkazian witchcraft, the Vampire defender sabotaged the raiders' military hardware and ran his weapon through the chest of the raid leader, forcing the latter to call for retreat. Currently, the raider leader has gone into hiding and Seš'qa is maintaining constant vigilance to track him down. 
Seš'qa regarded Jakub's betrayal as its responsibility. The latest news revealed that the leadership of the floating city is planning to create an organization dedicated to fighting crimes involving Sarkazian witchcraft and apprehending the traitors.

"Suffering will end. There shall be peace ... for all Sarkaz..."
The ancient Sarkaz mulled over these words as he cleaned the Arts Unit in his hand. Surrounding him was an endless stream of tourists who came with loved ones and friends. Liches created spectacular displays of fireworks with their Arts while children clambered on the Gargoyle warriors. People of every creed and tribe and race cheered, just as they did on the day when Seš'qa took to the skies, and on every Open Day that celebrated the end of the war.
"Is this ... our 'Suffering's End'...?"
The ancient Sarkaz packed his belongings quickly. He had already saved enough T-Creds to travel to various Band cities. For years he had planned to leave Seš'qa and visit the Civilization Band.

The journey was smooth and without event till that very day. He was lying on a giant boulder to gaze at the stars when the Originium coffee kettle suddenly switched itself off with a resounding snap. He was initially confused until he heard explosions, shouting, and screaming.
With alert eyes he gazed at the spreading hazefyre. A family of three was fleeing across the wilderness on foot while a mob of thirty mottled figures bearing arms chased after them. Landbreakers. The ancient Sarkaz witnessed the pursuit ... and did nothing. He laid himself back to rest again.

He was simply too old, and too ordinary. He was neither a Gargoyle blessed with a constitution as sturdy as a bastion, nor a Lich wielding esoteric and deadly Arts, nor a Nachzehrer with their terrifying and impossible strengths. He was simply a mixed Sarkaz lucky enough to outlive the Aggeloi War, the Humiliation War, and the Jakubine War that crushed the Warlord of the Wilds. The odd tricks of survival were the only thing he knew.
But barely a dozen seconds passed when the Sarkaz took out his Arts Unit and leaped down from the great boulder. He remembered the mad Speaker who gave a speech and promise to the Sarkaz, a piece of oratorical text that was obviously not written by herself. Nevertheless, there is something that never changes. If suffering were to end, someone has to do something about it.
He gently cleaned his Arts Unit. The chassis reflected the face of a Sarkaz who had aged far, far beyond yesteryear.

An arrow buried itself in the fleeing father who carried his child. Both collapsed to the ground. The woman threw away her comm device and tried to drag her man to safety. It was in vain. The breakers were upon them. The night in the wilderness instantly grew silent.
The breakers howled and laughed as they approached the stricken family from all sides. Mercilessly they raised their weapons. The man and woman tried, in vain, to shield their child. Torchlight glinted off the sabers, crossbow bolts, as well as the tears of the poor kid.
A great shadow wearing two horns suddenly appeared behind the breakers. With neither sound nor warning, a blackness darker than the night spread across the scene. One by one it seized the breakers who howled with despair as life was snuffed out of them. The rest of them were terrified. Desperately they searched to find where the unannounced attack came from. Words echoing in the night breeze found them first, words spoken in old, raspy Sarkazian —
"My suffering has ended. But yours ... has just begun."

This was Adelheid's first culture shock. 
Seš'qa, the Stop, the capital of Witchcraft, the Sarkazian hub, the gathering spot of vagabonds... It was a city of names and she heard plenty of them. However, it was not until she alighted from the dirigible and stepping onto Seš'qa proper when she realized that "flight" was the most insignificant feature of this strange realm. 
The entire place seemed to be a never-ending stream of carnivals. Riot was engraved into the air itself. The decorative furnace that adorned the central plaza spewed waves of heat, clamor, and tons of laughter. Every street was lined with strange shops and signs. People rubbed shoulders in the crowd, chewing food with names that defy even the most dexterous tongues as they marched for the formation of giant figures looming in the distance — Rumors speak of a fighting arena as well as a fairground featuring Sarkazian culture, meticulously prepared for tourists when Seš'qa made itself available to them. However, the purpose of this administrative divisions seems rather limited when Seš'qa itself was already like a giant theme park. 
Adelheid's stomach started rumbling again. 
Perhaps it wasn't a good idea to accept that wandering peddler's invitation. She heard about Witching Hour, but she could never afford anything from this manufacturer. She only needed a broom to chase away the beasts back home. Like Seš'qa itself, the concept of proper weapons felt foreign and distant. "But I only flipped a truck toppled by the Aggeloi so it got back on its wheels. Why would anyone recommend me a job opportunity for that?" Adelheid started to wonder. What could she possibly do at this place? 
The peddler was far away, handling some registration procedure, stringing syllables and words that she could not understand. She suddenly realized that she knew nothing about the Sarkaz, despite being one herself. And is that powerful mercenary a Goliath? A man wore pendants dangling from his sharp ears. Did they mean anything? Everything was new. The peddler explained that her constant sense of hunger was a racial trait as well. But knowing this did not solve the problem. According to Sarkazian standards, her stubborn refusal to "feed" probably made her the one least qualified to talk about the rebellious nature of this city. 
Her stomach rumbled louder. Every time she felt afraid or helpless, impulse would find its way in and make it harder to control herself. And this was worse than usual. If someone asks, how should she answer? It would be inappopriate to say: "I'm sorry. I just don't feel like being a Nachzehrer."
There was still a chance to escape. The peddler's route would pass through a few more towns and villages. She could always apologize later. It would be best to find a place to hide and wait for the constant sideway glances to ease off... 
"What's happening to you?" 
The voice jolted her back from her increasingly sticky sense of anxiety. The lad tilted his head, his gaze more curious than confused: "There's free bread over there. Just tell the guard before you grab one. And there's also a pamphlet with a list of jobs. That's free, too." 
"I ... I'm sorry, I'm actually alright," she tried to get her breathing under control and ease the trembling out of her voice, "I'm just waiting for someone." 
"Oh. Okay, " the lad sniveled, "But you don't have to worry. Plenty of opportunities here. You'll find something to do. It took me two whole weeks as well." 
The lad was mature for his age and did not seem to believe in her words. Adelheid thought about it but chose not to argue. His expressions seem to exude strange powers that alleviated her worries. 
He gave her a pat on the shoulders before blending into a nearby crowd once more. She turned to look. It did not appear like a tourist attraction. Sweaty laborers worked on the scaffold as merchants frowned and wrote out their orders. A few well-dressed individuals flanked by mercenaries walked out of what seemed to be a fancy bistro. Everyone looked busy, yet all of them gave off the same relaxing vibe of that young lad. There were plenty of opportunities and she would figure something out. 
She saw the lad running towards the mercenaries, shouting angrily as he bundled their weapons. He was like a shepherd trying to herd a flock of giant, half-drunken beasts from their masters into the inn. The lad's tail was short and sharp, reminding her of her foster parents. 
The girl suddenly remembered the peddler saying something on the dirigible: "We got it to fly because the Sarkaz everywhere were facing difficulties. But when it started flying, we realized that plenty of others are facing hard times, not just the Sarkaz." 
Before it became a flying city of amusements, Seš'qa was a frontier outpost. Despite being involved with countless legends and serving numerous functions, it was a young outpost facing the unknown in the frontiers where humanity strove to build a new home. Life will always find a way. The outpost does not need to house everyone. It just needs to be "a stop", and that would be enough. 
And thus, after more than ten minutes of shock and awe, Adelheid began diverting her attention to the streets. Her eyes rested upon a massive pile of roasted stockbeast fillet glistening with grease. 
It was salty, so salty that it sent her heart racing wildly.

Antal is not as cold or unsociable as he appears. Everyone who actually talked to him would agree with this statement. No one expected this stern-faced dude obsessed with Originium technology and sciences to be equally passionate about lame jokes! Why would this techie tell jokes so bad that one would need to devote all their brain juices and logical reasoning to fathom? Is he doing this to boost his sense of humor? When you look at his expression-less face and realize that he's doing his best to make you laugh, you might also find it difficult to determine why you end up laughing anyway. Is it because of his lame jokes? Or the stark contrast presented by his physical form? 
Akekuri, Antal's team captain, has maintained extreme optimism about this quirk: "At least he's sincere. Though there are times when he fails to read the context. For example, he may get a sudden urge to show off his sense of humor in the face of hostility. Unfortunately, the enemies often think otherwise." 
To Antal, "being someone interesting" may have become a lifelong pursuit, and he treats everyone as instructors capable of reviewing his performance. It doesn't matter if they are fellow teammates of Op Team Z7 or fellow Endfielders whom he only met once — Antal would humbly seek advice from anyone deemed capable of sharing valuable recommendations. 
Recently, Antal placed his antics on hold as a particular individual stepped up to the game and volunteered to offer constant feedback... Hold on. It's voluntary, right? I don't know if there are other people capable of laughing even before Antal finishes his bad jokes. Yes, we're talking about our Endministrator, who would, with the greatest patience, hang out with Antal, and listen to everything he has to say — ranging from eureka moments of inventive ideas to hour-long science lectures that he suddenly initiates when he finds an opportunity to do so. In a particular memorable moment, Antal tried to persuade the Endmin to take off the mask. His excuse was to apply certain mods like a pair of beam-firing eyes... Of course, Akekuri happened to be nearby and she fiercely reprimanded Antal's action. The Operator was forced to write a 6000-word self-examination essay and read it aloud before the Endmin on the following day. 
Of course, this punishment was hardly effective to Antal. It would only take a few days before his creative mind starts to formulate other interesting ideas.

Reconvener and Operator Laevatain joined Endfield with the Endministrator's direct recommendation. After acquiring her personal agreement, as well as approval from the HR Division and authentication from Rhodes Island, Laevatain joined Endfield as an operator under the direct command of the Endministrator. 

Laevatain arrived at the reception area a full 45 minutes ahead of the agreed-upon schedule. She simply placed the employment notification on the table and said little else except, "I'm here. We can begin." 
She was quite cooperative during the initial phase of the interview — giving her signature, submitting a retinal scan, and linking her Protocol Authority Level without a single fuss or comment. I tried to liven up the atmosphere by saying, "Welcome to Endfield." She nodded and replied, "I'm already here." 
During job-inclination testing, I followed the prescribed list of questions and asked if she considered utilizing her skill set in other non-combat roles, such as combat planner, coach, or instructor. She did not say anything but appeared obviously annoyed. 
In the end, Operator Laevatain left with this final line: "Just let me go to as many places you can — places that let me build as much memories as I can." 
— Martin Marvin Malen, Assistant, HR Division, Endfield Industries

"Endmin! Please help me keep Mi Fu occupied for a day!" It was late at night when Yan Ning paid a sudden visit to the Endministrator for an extremely urgent business. 
According to Yan Ning, she saw a sealed letter to be sent to Mi Fu while she was cleaning Zhuang Fangyi's desk. She thus took it upon herself to mail it to the Watchguard's barracks. 
But she quickly learned that the letter was not meant to be delivered at once. In Yan Ning's words: "If Mi Fu reads the letter before the hour intended by Fangyi, things could get really bad! Please keep Mi Fu distracted while I intercept the letter's delivery!" 
And hence, the Endministrator used the excuse of "live auditing" and kept Mi Fu company for the entirety of her daily shift. 
It began early in dawn when a traveling merchant surrounded by the Aggeloi called for help. Captain Mi then spent the entire morning mercilessly training the new watchguards. In the afternoon, she had to arbitrate disputes between shop owners of Fangxing Avenue followed by an unexpected encounter of the "Supreme Chief" at the bamboo grove... Mi Fu's fists never rested, yet they remained effective as always. 
Her restless shift finally ended when the sun has finally set and night took over. Still the Endministrator remained as Yan Ning has not yet intercepted or retrieved the letter. 
Back at the watchguard barracks, Mi Fu turned on the desk lamp and began filling in the procedural files and records under its warm, yellow glow. The wind outside made whistling sounds. She suddenly lowered her pen and headed outside, but saw nothing but loose leaves carried in the breeze. The Captain had felt rather restless on this day. 
Mi Fu returned to her desk and closed the case files. From her pocket she took out a letter from the Main Pillar Office, creased and soaked in sweat. She had signed and accepted it in the morning but never found time to read it. 

DOCUMENT: A Letter Not Intended for Delivery 
Mi Fu: 
I'm probably already on my way by the time you read this letter. In the event that I do not make it back, I will be counting on you to handle all public safety and administrative affairs of Wuling City. 
You have accompanied Wuling in every step. You were there when it was just a simple construction site in the wilderness and stayed till it became a city with beautiful buildings and orderly roads. You toiled with the construction crew, stood the night watch, and kept trouble at bay with your fists. I know your ties to Wuling run deep, and this is why I entrust this heavy duty to you. 
You never shied away from duty or responsibility. That is your strength. But your temper lacks patience and is obstinate. I understand this is part of your character, but the task of defending a city goes beyond fighting off enemies and winning battles. It requires tact and mindfulness. Deliberating and acting with prudence are not signs of weakness, but measures taken to guarantee success and give me a peace of mind. 
There is also the matter of Qingbo Stockade. This subject pulls you taut and tense. Meeting fellow Stockaders seems to ignite your fuse, but I know you have been struggling to act with mercy. Some people might not know the truth, but I see it clearly. It is nothing to be ashamed of. You have every right to be a friend of Tangtang without feeling the need to keep it a secret. 
And remember when I advised you to practice calligraphy? At first I was hoping it could improve your patience, but your words turned out just as stern and unyielding as your fists, and assumed a beauty of their own. The lessons are no longer necessary, but of course, if you find calligraphy enjoyable and have the leisure of time, seek Tianshi Ge for advice. There is no need to bring Tangyou Baba to him. His health no longer allows them in his diet. 
You often said how you had enough sweets for your lifetime and never wanted to see them again because sweetness now makes you sick. But I believe otherwise. There is no need to avoid what you like. Duty is heavy and taxing. Rare are the opportunities of personal happiness, and tiny indulgences should be kept available. A piece or two every now and then will do no harm. 
Finally, I have a few personal words to say to you. What I wanted to give you most is not this city, but yourself. You were a young girl with a fiery gaze when I first met you. In a single blink you charged straight for me with a fist poised to strike. But years have passed. You took on greater responsibilities, your fists became more merciless, and your frowns never eased. I have not seen your true self for a while. 
So remember, if there comes a day when you feel unhappy and work becomes a chore, then just leave it at that. Do not feel beholden to anyone and just ignore what the others say. Go wherever you like. Head back to the Stockade or travel across Talos-II. You can even choose to do nothing. You owe Wuling nothing, and thus you should be free. 
Take care of yourself. Smile and laugh when the time is right. 

Zhuang Fangyi

Lemme introduce an old friend of mine. Wait... Yeah. I think we're old friends. Anyway, the story begins with my least favorite angling style — Drop-n-Yank. 
Drop-n-Yank is just like what it says. No lures, no baits, and no waiting for the fins to bite. Drop the hook, yank with all your might, and hope it stabs into something that you can plop in the bucket. They call it angling, but it feels more like violent muggery to me — Absolutely zero patience or technique. One hundred percent deadly. 
I saw the technique for the first time at an abandoned wharf. An old angler with scars all over his face dropped, yanked, and man, it was aquatic murder. Blood everywhere and the poor fin was still flapping. A bunch of kids and I learned how to drop-n-yank by hiding behind the barrels while chewing on tortillas. 
That was how I "met" my old friend. It was my first time doing the drop-n-yank and I pulled the thing up from the water. But it fought back and tore itself free. I couldn't forget that bloody wound and the disfigured eye. Ugh. I can still feel that eye staring at me. Of course, I didn't bother with human-fin relations back then. People have to angle when they get hungry, and we can't help it when things get ugly. 
When I was a punk kid, we lived like fins stuffed in a can. First thing we do in the morning was a headcount to see who survived and who got "devoured" by the streets. Stealing, mugging, and lying? Those were the survival techniques. We negotiated with fists. When you have to drop-n-yank for fins, you know how rough it was back in those days. 
Then some guy showed up. One that didn't treat us like feral wildlings. He taught us how to negotiate properly, how to step back a little, and how to protect those around us. He even handed me La Estrada. Told me that someone has to do something different for the city. I believed him, you know. Maybe I can clean up the biz and make a name for myself. 
Nights got real quiet in those days. I would sometimes angle for fins at the wharf. That was when I saw it again. It became a great fin. The monstrous thing always fought back, always broke free, and always swam its victory circle. It was laughing at me with that ring of ripples. 
So I fought with people in the day and the fin at night. And it lasted till ... my two most trusted friends gave me "Game of Gangs the Reality Show" plus a ton of backstabbing. They were like two insane raptorfins trying to off each other, and I paid an eye to get them to stop. On the day when the gang broke up, I sat at the wharf to see the waves breaking against the wall. We painted graffiti together as kids. Now there was nothing but froth. Our friendship became a dead fin. Scaled and scraped clean. 
That was also the day when I realized it had become an old geezerfin — Old dude also lost a lot of weight and its scales were falling off. The injured eye had already turned entirely white. It leaped out of the water and stared at me coldly. It was laughing at me and telling me how I deserved everything. I thought it was our last meeting. 
But just two days ago, I ran into the geezerfin during night angling after I closed shop — It was full moon and I knew old geezerfin bit the hook. Man, I know that deadly strength anywhere. The battle felt like it lasted a hundred years. You should have seen the splashes. Feels like Maymay testing out her explosives underwater. But I was the victor of the struggle. The line did not snap and I hoisted geezerfin out of the water. It looked way bigger than it did during its prime. I was about to lower it in the fin crate when I saw that — there was nothing on the hook. Even the bait was still intact. 
Did I actually hook the thing? Did it just come and leave? Or was it just my unresolved angst and dilemmas that used the cover of night to show themselves? I finally understood when the last ripples disappeared. "It" was no longer a simple fin. 
It had become my lingering disappointments and obsession, an embodiment of "what ifs" left behind whenever I see someone leaving or dying early. I even toyed with the idea using the Originium Arts to "hook" it out in its entirety — I knew its form, its wounds, its actions, and even the way it stares at people. It's living with me, and it's way more alive than it had been in water.
